payload.author: devteamaegis
payload.body:
## What breaks

`split_url_and_private_token()` in `posthog/plugins/utils.py` (line 186) crashes with \`ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)\` when a plugin URL contains more than one \`?\` character. This function is called by \`parse_github_url\`, \`parse_gitlab_url\`, and \`parse_npm_url\`, so the crash surfaces at any plugin installation or validation endpoint that accepts user-supplied URLs.

## How to trigger

```python
from posthog.plugins.utils import split_url_and_private_token
split_url_and_private_token("https://github.com/PostHog/plugin?private_token=abc?extra")
# ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)
```

## Traceback

```
File "posthog/plugins/utils.py", line 186, in split_url_and_private_token
    url, query = url.split("?")
ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)
```

## Root cause

`url.split("?")` on line 186 returns more than 2 elements when the URL contains two or more `?` characters. The two-variable unpacking `url, query = ...` then raises `ValueError`.

## Fix

Change `url.split("?")` to `url.split("?", 1)` so the split stops at the first `?`, producing exactly two parts regardless of how many `?` chars appear in the URL.
payload.title: BUG: ValueError: too many values to unpack in split_url_and_private_token() when URL contains multiple '?' characters

## Repro

When connecting to the hosted MCP server `https://mcp.posthog.com/mcp` with
`?features=` query param, adding `dashboards` causes the OAuth flow to fail with
`error=invalid_scope` on the redirect callback. Other feature combinations work.

### Working scope sets (OAuth completes, MCP tools load)

- `?features=sql,data_schema`
- `?features=sql,data_schema,insights`

### Failing scope set

- `?features=sql,data_schema,insights,dashboards`
- Result: `http://localhost:<port>/callback?error=invalid_scope&state=<state>` (no `error_description`)

### Account context

- PostHog Cloud US, free tier, single project (id 443630), org "Ezequiel Machado"
  (id 019e6c40-af7a-0000-8804-a3afd3a460c8). Role: organization owner.
- Client: Claude Code (CLI), OAuth client metadata
  `https://claude.ai/oauth/claude-code-client-metadata`.

### Investigation

Inspected source:
- `services/mcp/schema/tool-definitions.json` lists features
  `data_warehouse, debug, events, experiments, feedback, insights, llm_analytics,
  notebooks, replay, search, surveys, workspace` — **no `dashboards`**.
- `services/mcp/definitions/core.yaml` has `dashboard-*` and `dashboard-templates-*`
  tools all marked `enabled: false`.
- `products/dashboards/mcp/tools.yaml` defines `dashboard-create/update/delete/get/...`
  with scopes `dashboard:read`, `dashboard:write`, `query:read` — these ARE in
  Claude Code's pre-registered OAuth scope list (visible in the failing URL's
  `scope=` param), so the request is otherwise valid.
- FAQ at `posthog.com/docs/model-context-protocol/faq` documents `dashboards`
  as a valid feature value.

Best guess: `dashboards` is documented as a public feature but its routing in
the MCP server still rejects users (maybe via feature flag, plan check, or
incomplete migration from the legacy core.yaml registry). The `invalid_scope`
error code is misleading — actual scope list is fine.

### Expected

Either:
- `?features=dashboards` succeeds for free-tier org owners and exposes
  `dashboard-create / dashboard-get / dashboards-get-all` tools, OR
- FAQ removes `dashboards` from the documented feature list until the routing
  is enabled.
payload.title: MCP: invalid_scope OAuth error when ?features= includes "dashboards"

payload.author: johnleonard1
payload.body:
## Summary

The MCP tool **`file-download-batch-exports-create`** exposes an `inputSchema` whose **root** is an `anyOf`. The Anthropic Messages API rejects any tool `input_schema` that uses `oneOf`/`allOf`/`anyOf` **at the top level**, so this one tool breaks the entire PostHog MCP integration for Anthropic-API-backed clients (Claude Desktop, Claude Code).

## Impact

Because clients send all connected tools in a single `tools` array, one invalid schema fails the **whole request** — not just calls to this tool. Every model turn 400s with:

```
API Error: 400 tools.N.custom.input_schema: input_schema does not support oneOf, allOf, or anyOf at the top level
```

In Claude Code specifically, this breaks all built-in subagents (`Explore`/`general-purpose`/`Plan`) that eager-load connector tools — they can't start at all. The only user-side workaround is manually blocking this single tool in connector settings. Verified against the live tool catalog on 2026-05-28: `file-download-batch-exports-create` is the **only** PostHog MCP tool with a top-level union (every sibling has an `{"type":"object"}` root and works fine).

## Root cause

In `services/mcp/src/tools/generated/batch_exports.ts`:

```ts
const FileDownloadBatchExportsCreateSchema = FileDownloadBatchExportsCreateBody   // union → anyOf at root
// vs the sibling, which is object-rooted:
const FileDownloadBatchExportsRetrieveSchema = FileDownloadBatchExportsRetrieveParams.omit({ project_id: true })
```

`FileDownloadBatchExportsCreateBody` is a union type, which `zod-to-json-schema` renders as a top-level `anyOf`. (Source: `products/batch_exports/mcp/tools.yaml` → generated `batch_exports.ts`.)

## Suggested fix

Guarantee that every MCP tool `inputSchema` has a `{"type":"object"}` root. For a union request body, wrap the union under a single object property, e.g.:

```jsonc
{ "type": "object", "properties": { "body": { "anyOf": [ ... ] } }, "required": ["body"] }
```

(Nested `anyOf` is accepted by the Anthropic API — only the top level is rejected.) A generator-level guard that wraps/flags any top-level non-object schema for MCP `inputSchema` would prevent this whole class of breakage.

## Environment

- Client: Claude Desktop / Claude Code (Anthropic Messages API)
- Observed: 2026-05-28
payload.title: MCP tool `file-download-batch-exports-create` has a top-level `anyOf` input_schema → breaks Anthropic API clients (Claude Desktop/Code)

payload.author: haacked
payload.body:
## Summary

Every server-side SDK auto-fires a `$feature_flag_called` event when you evaluate a flag with a `distinct_id`, and none of them mark that event as personless (`$process_person_profile = false`). Ingestion treats an event as personful whenever a `distinct_id` is present and nothing says otherwise, so any `distinct_id` that has no other events ends up with a person profile created from the flag-called event alone.

You see this most with backend services that evaluate flags across a large or short-lived set of `distinct_id`s. Those IDs never send a `pageview` or `identify`, so the flag-called event is the only thing that ever creates their profile. The result is a pile of empty, orphaned profiles that cost storage and person volume but tell you nothing.

## How profiles get created today

Ingestion defaults an event to personful and only backs off when `$process_person_profile` is explicitly `false`:

- `nodejs/src/ingestion/event-processing/normalize-process-person-flag-step.ts:29` sets `let processPerson = true // The default.`
- Only a literal `false` (or the `force_disable_person_processing` header) turns it off (same file, lines 37-43).

So a `$feature_flag_called` event with a `distinct_id` and no `$process_person_profile=false` is personful, and `processPersonsStep` creates or updates a person even when the event carries no `$set` properties at all.

## Cross-SDK status

No server SDK sets `$process_person_profile=false` on the auto-fired `$feature_flag_called` event:

| SDK | Auto-fires flag-called | `send_feature_flag_events` default | Sets `$process_person_profile=false`? | Dedups |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Python | yes | `true` | No | yes (distinct+key+value) |
| PHP | yes | `true` | No | yes (distinct+key) |
| Ruby | yes | `true` | No | yes (distinct+key+value) |
| Go | yes | `true` | No | yes (LRU) |
| .NET | yes | `true` | No | yes (sliding) |
| Elixir | yes | no opt-out | No | no dedup |
| Node (server) | yes | `true` | No (only when distinct_id absent) | yes (distinct+key+response) |

A couple of notes:

- The browser SDK (`posthog-js`) defaults to `personProfiles: 'identified_only'`, so anonymous client-side flag-called events are already personless. The Node server client is stateless and doesn't inherit that, so it captures flag-called events as personful like the rest of the server SDKs.
- Elixir is the worst case. It has no dedup and no way to turn flag-called events off.

## Why it surfaces now

The behavior has always been there, but normal usage hides it:

- Most server flag-evals use real `distinct_id`s that already have a profile from client-side activity, so the flag-called event just attaches to the existing person and no orphan appears.
- Per-process dedup keeps the volume down (one event per distinct_id, flag, and value).
- The browser path, which is where most flag evaluation happens, is already personless for anonymous users.

It only gets expensive when a backend evaluates flags across a lot of `distinct_id`s that never do anything else.

## Proposed fix

Force `$feature_flag_called` events personless at ingestion, in `normalize-process-person-flag-step.ts`, instead of fixing each SDK:

- One change covers every SDK and every version already deployed, right away.
- Personless still attaches to a person when one exists. The personless path stamps the canonical `person_id` if there's already a person for the `distinct_id` (`process-personless-step.ts:50-87`), and the `personless_distinct_id` and `force_upgrade` machinery reconciles the anonymous-then-identified case afterward. The browser SDK already relies on this path, so experiment exposure-to-conversion joins keep working for identified users.

### Trade-offs and open questions

There are two things to settle before shipping this. First, `personProfiles: 'always'` clients deliberately asked for personful flag-called events, and an unconditional ingestion rule would override them. The SDK always writes `$process_person_profile` explic
payload.title: bug(flags):Orphaned person profiles created via $feature_flag_called event

payload.author: MattBro
payload.body:
## Goal

Publish the public discovery surface for agentic provisioning so partners and agents following the MCP / auth.md convention can self-serve onboard via CIMD without bespoke per-partner documentation.

Three artifacts:

1. **`posthog.com/auth.md`**. Open agent-registration protocol doc. References the CIMD `com.posthog.scopes` namespace (#60334), points at the provisioning endpoints (`/api/provisioning/account_requests`, `/api/provisioning/oauth/token`, `/api/provisioning/resources`), and documents the PKCE + consent and PKCE + email-claim flows.
2. **`/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`**. RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata pointing at the AS, with `scopes_supported`, `bearer_methods_supported`. We currently only serve `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` and `/.well-known/jwks.json`. Should align with the existing MCP-side PRM at `services/mcp/src/hono/public-routes.ts:48`, which already advertises `authorization_servers: ["https://posthog.com"]`. The two protected resources (provisioning API + MCP) share one authorization server; no contradictions between the two PRMs.
3. **`agent_auth` block**. Added to the existing `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` response, describing supported registration methods (pkce + consent for unknown users, pkce + email-claim for new users, future id-jag).

## Why now

The provisioning backend (`ee/api/agentic_provisioning/`) and CIMD client-registration path (`posthog/api/oauth/cimd.py`) already implement the substantive backend. Discovery is the missing surface. Without it, only partners we hand-hold can find the flow. Publishing flips agentic provisioning from a per-partner integration into an open protocol any CIMD-registered partner or agent can self-serve onto.

CIMD was adopted by the IETF OAuth WG (Oct 2025) and is the preferred default for MCP client registration as of the Nov 2025 spec. We're already on the right side of the standard; this issue is publishing the artifacts an agent following the convention expects to find.

## Hard dependencies

This issue should not land until the provisioning↔MCP token bridge is functional and CIMD partners have a way to declare their scope set. The auth.md doc references both, and the discovery surface advertises them.

**Bridge functionality** (the "register once, use MCP" claim depends on this):
- [ ] #60477. `OAuthApplication.scopes` foundation.
- [ ] #60329 (I1). Per-app scope ceiling enforced at `/authorize`.
- [ ] #60331 (I3). Same enforcement on the provisioning direct-mint path (`ee/api/agentic_provisioning/views.py:997`).

**CIMD scope declaration** (auth.md's "Pick a method" section references this):
- [ ] #60343 (C1). CIMD partner heads-up sent.
- [ ] #60334 (I6). CIMD `com.posthog.scopes` nested namespace.

**Partner readiness** (so the doc matches what new partners actually receive):
- [ ] #60343 (C1). Insforge heads-up sent.
- [ ] #60332 (I4). Default-off provisioned PAT, so the auth.md "Use the credential" section accurately describes the default response shape.

### Why these specifically

Without #60329 + #60331, the "register once, use MCP" headline fails the first time a partner tries any MCP tool outside the ~7-scope overlap between `StripeIntegration.SCOPES` (`posthog/models/integration.py:3297`) and the union of scopes declared across `products/*/mcp/tools.yaml`. Reading the code on both sides:

- MCP's `hasScope` (`services/mcp/src/lib/api.ts:1`) does literal scope-string matching with a write→read fallback. No wildcard.
- Provisioning's default token carries 15 scopes; the partner-requestable allowlist (`ALLOWED_PROVISIONING_SCOPES`, `ee/api/agentic_provisioning/views.py:2134`) is 18; the MCP tool surface needs ~80. Overlap is 7-8.

So most MCP tools refuse a provisioning-issued token today. RFC #1103 / #60327 fixes the root cause (per-app ceiling, empty → `UNPRIVILEGED_SCOPES` broad default), not the tactical hand-curated allowlist.

Without #60334, the auth.md "Pick a method" section would have to d
payload.title: feat(oauth): publish auth.md discovery surface for agent registration

payload.author: andehen
payload.body:
## Background

Follow-up from review of [#60380](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/60380), which fixed an unconditional `toUInt8(...)` failure in the funnel events precomputation INSERT (`experiment_metric_events_preaggregated`).

That bug had been failing **every** matching INSERT in production (deterministically, ~3.8k warns/24h) yet wasn't surfacing as a user-visible problem. The reason: there is a fallback path — when precomputation fails, the query runner falls back to the "direct" path and still returns results. So a complete, deterministic failure of the precomputation path was effectively invisible.

## Problem

The fallback is good for resilience, but it masks errors. A precomputation path can be 100% broken and we'd never notice because results keep coming back via the direct path — just slower and without the precomputation benefit. We only caught this one because of the log noise.

## What we should do

- **Make these errors propagate / surface.** A precomputation failure shouldn't be silently swallowed by the fallback — it should be observable (alerting, error reporting, or surfaced metrics) so we know when the precomputation path is broken even though the fallback keeps queries working.
- **Improve observability** around the precomputation vs. direct path — e.g. track how often the fallback is being hit and why, so a systematic failure stands out instead of blending into normal retry noise.

(Discussed further in the Slack thread.)

cc @lricoy
payload.title: Experiment metric precomputation failures are silently masked by the direct-path fallback

Part of #60327 — implements [RFC #1103](https://github.com/PostHog/requests-for-comments-internal/pull/1103).

**Cross-cutting. Rollout checklist; per-slice unit/contract tests live in their own slices.**

### E2E manual matrix (run both US + EU)
| Flow | Assert |
|---|---|
| Wizard install | Old CLI sending the list → exact grant (app seeded as superset, no reject); rolled-forward CLI omitting `scope=` → seeded set |
| Stripe Projects install | Resolves the pre-provisioned app by id; hard-fails if missing; token carries contracted set |
| DCR client (Cursor) | No `scope=` → `UNPRIVILEGED_SCOPES`; hardcoded privileged `scope=` → `invalid_scope` |
| Agentic provisioning + provisioned PAT | PAT inherits `application.scopes` (not `["*"]`); downstream wizard call succeeds on seeded scopes |
| Gateway call w/ + w/o `llm_gateway:read` | With → 200; without → 403 |
| Third-party widening re-consent | Email + approval page bumps only the approving user's tokens; refresh carries wider set forward (#54277) |
| First-party widening | Transparent bump, no email/approval |

### Note
Invariant tests for scope-name drift are already tracked and ship independently: #57525, #57526, #57534, #57535. Link, don't recreate.

Part of #60327 — implements [RFC #1103](https://github.com/PostHog/requests-for-comments-internal/pull/1103).

**Phase 4 — strictly ordered internally. Lands last.**

### Scope (in order)
1. Roll the PostHog Code CLI forward to omit `scope=` instead of sending `["*"]` (overlaps I13's roll-forward).
2. Data-migrate existing `OAuthAccessToken` rows whose scope is `*` onto the resolved explicit set, so they keep working — **must precede I2's `get_original_scopes` override** or that override must be `*`-aware (a `*` token intersected with the ceiling yields `{}` and gets rejected). These are the 7-day-TTL DCR/CIMD sessions.
3. Only then remove the `*` short-circuit in `APIScopePermission` (`posthog/permissions.py:507`) and reject `scope=*` at `/authorize`. Also handle `*` in `downgrade_scopes_to_read_only` (`posthog/scopes.py`) and the SCOPES dict.

### Validation
- `posthog/test/test_permissions.py` wildcard cases; migration test that `*` rows convert; `/authorize?scope=*` → `invalid_scope`.


### Gate: seed the PostHog Code desktop app (precedes step 1)

The PostHog Code **desktop** OAuth app (US + EU, the `ARRAY_APP_CLIENT_ID_US/EU` clients, a.k.a. `POSTHOG_CODE_US/EU_APP_ID` in the gateway config) authorizes with `scope=["*"]` and has an empty `OAuthApplication.scopes` ceiling, so it rides the `*` grandfather. Retiring `*` drops its `llm_gateway:read` (privileged, never in the unprivileged default) and the gateway rejects it once #60340 lands. Seed its ceiling first.

- **Seed set:** `UNPRIVILEGED_SCOPES ∪ {llm_gateway:read}`, US + EU. Not a minimal list: the desktop agent proxies the user token to the PostHog MCP server, whose tools span the full unprivileged surface, so any subset would `403` some MCP tool. Exclude `llm_gateway:write` and hidden scopes.
- **Different from the Wizard gate (#60341):** Wizard sends an explicit list, so a superset ceiling accepts its old client. PostHog Code sends `*`, which a non-empty ceiling rejects at `/authorize` (`OAuthValidator.validate_scopes`). So seeding rejects old-CLI **fresh** logins until the CLI rolls forward; seed immediately before step 1, not as a free-standing prerequisite. Existing tokens refresh fine (the `*` passthrough in `get_original_scopes`) until the CLI bumps `OAUTH_SCOPE_VERSION`.
- **Ordering:** seed (US + EU) → step 1 (CLI roll-forward) → #60340 → step 2 (`*`-token migration) → step 3 (reject `scope=*`). Step 2 must run **after** the seed, or `*` resolves to the unprivileged default and migrated tokens lose `llm_gateway:read`.
- **Not affected:** the server-side direct-mint path (`create_oauth_access_token_for_user`) already carries `llm_gateway:read` and ignores the ceiling, so sandbox/background agents survive `*` retirement.

Part of #60327 — implements [RFC #1103](https://github.com/PostHog/requests-for-comments-internal/pull/1103).

**Phase 1.** Depends on PR #60477 (`OAuthApplication.scopes` + constants) for the Stripe grandfather, whose PAT inherits `application.scopes`. Triggers the Insforge heads-up in C1 #60343.

## Direction change: gate off by default, do not just narrow

Originally framed as narrowing the provisioned PAT from `scopes=["*"]` to `application.scopes`. A prod audit (2026-05-27) reframed the call to **gate minting off by default** and grandfather the one shipped consumer (Stripe).

Findings that drove it:
- Provisioned PATs are tiny in absolute terms (Stripe 42 keys, 20 ever used; Insforge 81 keys, 80 ever used in test / pre-launch usage), against ~26k user-created `["*"]` PATs in the wild that are independent of the provisioning flow.
- The wizard already drops the provisioned PAT (`wizard/src/utils/setup-utils.ts:577-584`).
- Insforge already runs OAuth refresh in production (~12k refresh exchanges, matching its app's refresh-token row count) and is pre-launch, so it can launch OAuth-only with no migration.
- The cheapest moment to remove a credential dependency is before partners ship on it. Default-off captures that window: Insforge and every future partner never receive a PAT; only Stripe (already shipped, published `.env` contract) needs real migration later.

## Scope

- Add `provisioning_issues_personal_api_key` (BooleanField, default `False`) to `OAuthApplication`. Generate the migration with `makemigrations`; run `analyze_migration_risk` and `makemigrations --check --dry-run`.
- `_create_provisioned_pat` (`ee/api/agentic_provisioning/views.py:1224`): thread the issuing app through (currently takes only `user, team`).
- Gate at both call sites:
  - `provisioning_resources_create` (`views.py:1516`), where `app = access_token.application` (`views.py:1441`).
  - `provisioning_rotate_credentials` (`views.py:1605`), via the same `_authenticate_bearer` handle.
- Grandfather: set `provisioning_issues_personal_api_key = True` on the legacy Stripe app (resolved by `STRIPE_POSTHOG_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`, see `_get_legacy_stripe_oauth_app`). For Stripe, `_create_provisioned_pat` replaces `scopes=["*"]` (`views.py:1251`) with `application.scopes`, preserving the narrowing where it still applies.

## Validation

- Update `ee/api/agentic_provisioning/test_resources.py:144` (asserts `pat.scopes == ["*"]`).
- New tests:
  - PAT is not minted when `provisioning_issues_personal_api_key = False` (the default), for both create and rotate.
  - `access_configuration` omits `personal_api_key` entirely when the flag is off.
  - When `True`, the PAT inherits `application.scopes` rather than `["*"]`.
payload.title: feat(provisioning): default-off provisioned PAT mint gate; Stripe grandfathered with application.scopes

Part of #60327 — implements [RFC #1103](https://github.com/PostHog/requests-for-comments-internal/pull/1103).

**Phase 1.** Depends on #60329 (foundation + `/authorize` enforcement).

### Scope
Drop `_validate_scopes` (`ee/api/agentic_provisioning/views.py:2130`) and `ALLOWED_PROVISIONING_SCOPES` (`:2108`, already contains `llm_gateway:read` at `:2118`). Apply `request ∩ application.scopes` (reject outside-ceiling) on **all three** issuance paths:
1. Consent path — builds an `/authorize` URL (`_build_authorize_url`), already flows through I1's override. ✓
2. **Direct-mint** — `_exchange_authorization_code` creates the token by hand (`views.py:995-1003`, `scope_str = " ".join(scopes) if scopes else StripeIntegration.SCOPES`). Never calls `OAuthValidator`; needs explicit intersection here.
3. **Provisioning refresh** — `_exchange_refresh_token` re-creates the token with `scope=old_scope` and no intersection; add narrowing.

`account_requests` reads `scopes` at `views.py:321`.

### Reconcile
The in-flight `worktree-scope-update-service` / `scope-update-followup` branches hydrate token scope at issuance/refresh (scope pinned to consent org). Reconcile this slice with that work before splitting code.

### Validation
- Rewrite/remove `ee/api/agentic_provisioning/test_scope_validation.py` (tests `_validate_scopes`).
- New cases in `test_account_requests.py`: in/out-of-ceiling on consent + direct-mint; refresh narrowing on the provisioning refresh path.


**Direct-mint bypass (load-bearing).** PR #60477 enforces the ceiling at `/authorize` via an `OAuthValidator.validate_scopes` override. That override does NOT reach `_exchange_authorization_code` at `ee/api/agentic_provisioning/views.py:997-1003`, which creates the token by hand with `OAuthAccessToken.objects.create(scope=scope_str, ...)`. The intersection (`request ∩ application.scopes`) has to land inline here just before the `create()` call, with the same OIDC carve-out (`OIDC_SCOPES ∪ {"introspection"}` always allowed). Same applies to `_exchange_refresh_token`. Three issuance paths total: consent path (already covered by /authorize override), direct-mint, refresh.

Part of #60327 — implements [RFC #1103](https://github.com/PostHog/requests-for-comments-internal/pull/1103).

**Phase 1.** Depends on PR #60477 (`OAuthApplication.scopes` + constants). Ordering-coupled to I14 (wildcard retirement).

> **Status (partially delivered):** the core `get_original_scopes` narrowing + tests shipped in #60477 ([7e4af8ffa00](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/commit/7e4af8ffa00d119f07b592941bd9844a52074478)); the accelerated revoke path shipped in #61711 (as `revoke_application_sessions`). What remains here is `*`-token narrowing (blocked on wildcard retirement #60342) and carrying the token name across refresh (deferred to its own slice).

### Scope

- [x] Override `get_original_scopes` on `OAuthValidator` (`posthog/api/oauth/views.py`; base is DOT `oauth2_validators.py:795`) to return `original_token.scopes ∩ application.scopes`. Caps every refresh at the app's current ceiling: a narrowed app drops removed scopes on next refresh. **Done in #60477** — OIDC/introspection pass through; empty ceiling is a no-op.
- [ ] **`*`-aware narrowing:** a `*` token must not intersect to `{}` (empty-scope tokens are rejected by `APIScopePermission`). #60477 leaves `*` tokens untouched as the interim behavior; true narrowing needs I14's `*`-token migration (#60342) to land first.
- [ ] Carry `OAuthAccessToken.name` across refresh so it persists for the connection's life. **Deferred to its own slice** — the naive `impersonated_by_id`-style mirror 500s (DOT's `RefreshToken.revoke()` nulls the FK before `_create_access_token`); a correct carry needs a `label` field on `OAuthRefreshToken`, and nothing sets `OAuthAccessToken.label` at mint yet.
- [x] Accelerated narrowing path: force-invalidate outstanding tokens. **Done in #61711** — shipped as `revoke_application_sessions(application)` (app-wide revoke of all AT/RT/grants) wired to a "Revoke all sessions" admin action on `OAuthApplicationAdmin`; guarded against a racing mint on the DOT, code-exchange, and provisioning/agentic paths.

### Validation

- [x] New tests: narrowed-app drops out-of-ceiling scopes next refresh; live `*` token survives one refresh; in-ceiling / empty-ceiling / zero-overlap cases. **Done in #60477** (`TestOAuthAPI.test_refresh_caps_scopes_at_app_ceiling` + `test_refresh_leaves_wildcard_token_untouched`), verified end-to-end against the oauthlib/DOT refresh path.
- [ ] `name` survives refresh (pairs with the name-carry item above).

**Why this stays separate from PR #60477's enforcement:** the refresh path in djoauth (`oauth2_provider/oauth2_validators.py:795` `get_original_scopes`) does not re-run `validate_scopes`. #60477 now overrides it so non-`*` tokens are capped at the ceiling on refresh, but existing `scope="*"` tokens keep refreshing into new `scope="*"` tokens — narrowing `*` is ordering-coupled to wildcard retirement (#60342) so `original ∩ application.scopes` doesn't empty a `*` token.

Part of #60327 — implements [RFC #1103](https://github.com/PostHog/requests-for-comments-internal/pull/1103).

**The first vertical slice. Ships the foundation *and* makes it do something end-to-end: seed an app's `scopes` in Django admin and that app's `/authorize` tokens are capped to it. Makes `llm_gateway:read` authoritative on the token.** Two PRs, in order.

## PR 1 — foundation (no behavior change; the other path slices depend on this PR landing)
- `posthog/scopes.py`: add `ALL_SCOPES` (does not exist today — define as the full `obj:action` string set from `API_SCOPE_OBJECTS` / `get_scope_descriptions()`), `PRIVILEGED_SCOPES = frozenset({"llm_gateway:read"})`, `HIDDEN_SCOPES` (rename of `OAUTH_HIDDEN_SCOPE_OBJECTS`, `posthog/scopes.py:130`; current value `{"wizard_session"}`), `UNPRIVILEGED_SCOPES = ALL_SCOPES - PRIVILEGED_SCOPES - HIDDEN_SCOPES`. Mind the string-vs-object-set arithmetic (hidden/internal are scope-objects, privileged are scope-strings). Decide whether OIDC/`introspection` belong in `UNPRIVILEGED_SCOPES`.
- `posthog/models/oauth.py`: `OAuthApplication.scopes` (`ArrayField(CharField(max_length=64), default=list, db_default=list, null=False)`; model at `:54`) and `OAuthAccessToken.name` (`CharField(max_length=255, blank=True, default="")`; model at `:280`).
- `posthog/admin/admins/oauth_admin.py`: add `scopes` to `OAuthApplicationForm` `get_fieldsets` (`:118-167`) so by-hand backfill works.
- Use `python manage.py makemigrations` (do not hand-write); confirm the ArrayField `db_default` renders `DEFAULT ARRAY[]::varchar[]`. Constants must import without Django (MCP scope codegen depends on it). **Ships as its own PR** per repo convention — fast review, de-risks PR 2.
- Validation: set-algebra unit tests (UNPRIVILEGED excludes hidden + privileged + internal); `analyze_migration_risk` clean; migrate green on `CLOUD_DEPLOYMENT=US` and `=EU`; existing rows default to `[]` / `""`.

## PR 2 — enforcement at `/authorize`
- Add a `validate_scopes` override to `OAuthValidator` (`posthog/api/oauth/views.py:170`; none today). Resolve `effective_scopes = request.client.scopes or UNPRIVILEGED_SCOPES`. **Keep OIDC scopes valid** (`openid/profile/email/introspection`; `DEFAULT_SCOPES = ["openid"]` at `posthog/settings/web.py:775`) — a naive `issubset` rejects them.
- Resolution rule: omit / empty / null `scope=` → grant `effective_scopes`; all requested in set → grant + echo (RFC 6749 §3.3); any value outside → reject with `invalid_scope`. On the GET branch this is a **redirect** carrying `error=invalid_scope`, not HTTP 400.
- Wire all three `create_authorization_response` calls: first-party auto-approve (`views.py:598`), consent-skip/auto (`:616`), POST (`:670`; `def post` at `:636`).
- Consent UI shows the **granted** set (`OAuthAuthorize.tsx:357-378`, currently off the raw requested `scope=` via `oauthAuthorizeLogic.ts:423`).
- Token-issuance audit entry `(application_id, source: explicit|broad_default, resolved_scopes, granted_scopes)` — **net-new wiring**; token mints are not logged today.
- Validation: `posthog/api/oauth/test_views.py` four resolution branches; empty-`scopes` app → `UNPRIVILEGED_SCOPES`; admin-set hidden scope validates (edge case 5); OIDC preserved; existing `invalid_scope` tests assert the redirect form (`test_views.py:2136`, `:2745`). Manual: seed a real app, ceiling enforced end-to-end.


---

## Implementation decision (post-research)

**Hook choice:** override `OAuthValidator.validate_scopes` at `posthog/api/oauth/views.py:170` (not `OAUTH2_PROVIDER["SCOPES_BACKEND_CLASS"]`). Both receive `application=request.client` and both run inside `create_authorization_response` before any grant or token row is written (`oauthlib/oauth2/rfc6749/grant_types/authorization_code.py:419`). The discriminator: `SCOPES_BACKEND_CLASS` also drives `views/base.py:162-163` (consent template's scope catalog) and `get_default_scopes` resolution via the `_DEFAULT_SCOPES` `__all__` branch (`oauth2_provider/settings.py:2

Part of #60327 — implements [RFC #1103](https://github.com/PostHog/requests-for-comments-internal/pull/1103).

**Phase 0 — foundation. Blocks every other slice. No behavior change.**

### Scope
- `posthog/scopes.py`: add `ALL_SCOPES` (does not exist today — define as the full `obj:action` string set built from `API_SCOPE_OBJECTS` / `get_scope_descriptions()`), `PRIVILEGED_SCOPES = frozenset({"llm_gateway:read"})`, `HIDDEN_SCOPES` (rename of `OAUTH_HIDDEN_SCOPE_OBJECTS`, `posthog/scopes.py:130`; current value is `{"wizard_session"}`), and `UNPRIVILEGED_SCOPES = ALL_SCOPES - PRIVILEGED_SCOPES - HIDDEN_SCOPES`. Watch the string-vs-object-set arithmetic: hidden/internal sets are scope-*objects*, `PRIVILEGED_SCOPES` is scope-*strings* — expand consistently. Decide whether OIDC/`introspection` scopes belong in `UNPRIVILEGED_SCOPES`.
- `posthog/models/oauth.py`: add `OAuthApplication.scopes` (`ArrayField(CharField(max_length=64), default=list, db_default=list, null=False)`) and `OAuthAccessToken.name` (`CharField(max_length=255, blank=True, default="")`). `OAuthApplication` is at `posthog/models/oauth.py:54`, `OAuthAccessToken` at `:280`.

payload.author: MattBro
payload.body:
Umbrella for implementing [RFC: Server-side scope assignment for OAuthApplications](https://github.com/PostHog/requests-for-comments-internal/pull/1103).

Move OAuth scope assignment from client-driven (`/authorize?scope=...`) to a server-stored ceiling on a new `OAuthApplication.scopes` field. Privileged scopes (`llm_gateway:read`) only land on the field via admin grant; self-serve channels (CIMD, DCR) are filtered.

## Corrections to the RFC (baked into the sub-issues, RFC doc left as-is)

A review pass against `master` (django-oauth-toolkit 3.2.0) found six claims that change the work:

1. **`validate_scopes` premise is half-wrong.** A global `OAUTH2_PROVIDER["SCOPES"]` already exists (`posthog/settings/web.py:755`) and DOT already rejects unknown scopes. The gap is a **per-application** ceiling, not "no enforcement."
2. **Provisioning has a direct-mint path that never hits `OAuthValidator`.** `_exchange_authorization_code` mints the token by hand (`ee/api/agentic_provisioning/views.py:997-1003`). Step 4 needs explicit intersection in three places (consent path, direct-mint, `_exchange_refresh_token`), not just dropping `_validate_scopes`.
3. **Wildcard ordering is a live-traffic hazard.** Naive `original ∩ application.scopes` on a `*` token yields `{}` and empty-scope tokens get rejected — and `*` tokens are the 7-day-TTL MCP sessions. The `*`-token migration must precede the `get_original_scopes` override, or the override must be `*`-aware.
4. **OIDC scopes must survive the override.** Every `/authorize` carries `openid`; a naive `issubset` rejects `openid/profile/email/introspection`.
5. **Activity-log claim is wrong.** There is **zero** activity-log wiring for `OAuthApplication` today (Django admin's `LogEntry` is not our activity log). Audit history + token-issuance audit are net-new build.
6. **No new Stripe env var.** `STRIPE_POSTHOG_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` already exists (`posthog/settings/integrations.py:85`) and `_get_legacy_stripe_oauth_app()` keys off it. Only change: drop create-on-demand, hard-fail.

Minor: `HIDDEN_SCOPES` example is `wizard_session` (not `user_interview_DO_NOT_USE`); `ALL_SCOPES` does not exist yet; `*` short-circuit is `posthog/permissions.py:507`; GET `/authorize` rejection is a redirect with `error=invalid_scope`, not HTTP 400.

## Sequencing

- **Phase 1** (foundation + enforcement + reads): I1 is PR #60477 — foundation (constants + schema) AND `/authorize` enforcement combined per the research recap on #60329. Then I2 #60330, I3 #60331, I4 #60332.
- **Phase 2** (write paths, parallel after I0): I5, I6, I7.
- **Phase 3** (frontend/UI): I8, I9, I10, and the widening flow tracked on #54277.
- **Phase 4** (cross-team + teardown, last): I12 (gateway, after I1 in prod), I13 (wizard), I14 (wildcard retire — strictly ordered).
- **Cross-cutting:** C1 (comms — CIMD heads-up before I6, Insforge before I4), T1 (e2e validation matrix). Invariant tests already tracked at #57525 / #57526 / #57534 / #57535 and ship independently.

Sub-issues are linked below.


## Index
- I1 #60329 (incl. foundation) · I2 #60330 · I3 #60331 · I4 #60332
- I5 #60333 · I6 #60334 · I7 #60335
- I8 #60336 · I9 #60338 · I10 #60339 · I11 #54277
- I12 #60340 · I13 #60341 · I14 #60342
- C1 #60343 · T1 #60344

## Related (not sub-issues)
- #62250 — email OTP ownership proof for existing-account linking in the provisioning flow (interacts with the scope ceiling: the minted token's scopes are capped by `OAuthApplication.scopes`)

payload.author: arthurdedeus
payload.body:
Data warehouse properties discussion ## What users need Users need to have a way to add custom data to their accounts. This data can be stuff like: - some link, some URL to other service - some configuration - some kind of last touch point - what kind of plan they're on - stuff like that On top of that, users should be able to add properties from connected data sources via Data Warehouse. If they are using Salesforce or Zendesk or HubSpot and they want to connect their data from these platforms into their accounts in PostHog, they should be able to do so via Data Warehouse. They sync the source data to Data Warehouse, and then we handle the connection for them so that the data is available for them to use in the accounts, to display on the list as a column, to filter, and to order the results based on those properties. The question that remains is how can we do all of this? ## Two patterns to figure out Doing some research, there is a pattern that applies for each of these situations: 1. How to handle custom properties and display them in a meaningful way in the UI 2. How to handle this data warehouse connection data, starting with the custom properties ## Pattern 1: Custom properties The idea is fundamentally what we already have in the accounts model, where we have a set of structured columns, which are the actual Postgres columns. We have columns that are used used across the board and a jsonb column, that in our case is the properties column, which is responsible for storing all these custom properties that the users add. For us to make sense out of these custom properties, the next part that we are missing is to have an external properties schema definition. This is pretty much a map from: - this is the property - this is the property type - this is how we display them in the UI - this is the last time it was synced and stuff like that All the metadata lives in this external schema definition, and this is pretty much what's missing for us to be able to provide this right now. ## Pattern 2: Connected warehouse data To handle the connected data, one pattern that stood out is the warehouse-native unification + reverse ETL. Which is a fancy way of saying that we: - sync everything into the data warehouse as-is, pretty much the data warehouse connections that we have built already - with custom SQL, we build the customer 360 view that gets pushed back into the account properties - and therefore needs to have an entry in the external property schema definition, but it will behave pretty much the same as a user-entered custom property. The only caveat is that it'll be updated periodically based on the customer 360 SQL. It's probably a materialized view or something like that. ## The dilemma (not Nelly's) ### tl;dr Another way to build this is with a query runner that merges Postgres and data warehouse tables. The worry is that the performance will be poor as we read more data. For simple lookups or filtering/ordering by values that live in Postgres, the query would be mostly built in Django ORM and only enriched (joined) with dhw data as a final step. This is the happy path. If we want to order/filter by fields that live in dwh, the start point of the query needs to be dwh. From the ordered/filtered set of accounts, we'd then query them in Postgres to get the remaining data and finally return the results.
## To Do - [x] MCP tools for CustomPropertyDefinition - [x] MCP tools for CustomPropertyValue - [x] Display custom properties in accounts list - [x] Display custom properties in account details - [x] CustomPropertyValues on Workflows - [x] CustomPropertyValues from materialized views
payload.title: Add custom properties to accounts

### Bug Description

## Please describe

When a user configures an Azure OpenAI provider key and selects an Azure model (e.g. gpt-4.1) in the playground, clicking `Run` results in `LLM Error: An internal error occurred.` The browser console shows:

`Provider key is for 'azure_openai' but request specifies 'openai'`

Looks like models like gpt-4.1 are registered in `OpenAIConfig.SUPPORTED_MODELS`, so `get_default_models()` returns them with `provider: "OpenAI"`. The playground UI correctly shows the Azure icon for the model when an Azure key is configured, but the `CompletionRequest` is constructed with `provider: "openai"` (from the model registry) rather than `provider: "azure_openai"` (from the key).

The validation in `Client._validate_provider()` then correctly rejects the mismatch between the key's provider (`azure_openai`) and the request's provider (`openai`), raising `ProviderMismatchError`.

Azure is also absent from the `PROVIDERS` list in `__init__.py`, which means `get_default_models()` can't returns Azure-specific entries. The `_get_provider()` function in `client.py` does handle `azure_openai` as a case, so the backend routing works; it's just the request construction that uses the wrong provider value.

## How to reproduce

1. Go to Settings > AI Observability (or LLM analytics) and add an Azure OpenAI provider key
2. Open the Playground
3. Select an Azure model (e.g. gpt-4.1, shown with Azure icon)
4. Enter any prompt and click Run
5. Observe "LLM Error: An internal error occurred"
6. Check browser console for: `Provider key is for 'azure_openai' but request specifies 'openai'`

## Additional context

### Feature request

The [workflow automation docs](https://posthog.com/docs/support/workflows) cover ticket management actions (status changes, SLA, assignment) but there's no native action for posting a reply into a conversation. This is a critical missing piece for AI-assisted support workflows.

Use case:

1. Trigger on $conversation_message_received
2. Call an external LLM via webhook to generate a draft reply
3. Post that reply back into the conversation

Step 3 currently has no supported path – the /compose/ endpoint blocks external API access (see related bug report), and there's no native workflow action for sending replies.

Proposed solution:

Add a native "Send reply" action under the Support section in the workflow builder, which accepts:

content – the message body (supports output variable references like {variables.draft_reply})
conversation – the ticket ID (can be pulled from {event.properties.ticket_id})
Optionally:

is_private – boolean to post as an internal note vs. customer-visible reply
Why this matters:

This closes the loop for AI-assisted support workflows entirely within PostHog, without requiring external API access or workarounds. The trigger, LLM call, and reply can all be orchestrated natively.

### Bug Description

Shift+M not working after opening demo.mov

Shift+M is handled by a document‑level keydown in App.tsx:2048-2216.
The demo window uses the YouTube player via MediaPlayer in index.tsx:1-16, which injects an iframe through the YouTube API in index.tsx:41-108.
When you click inside the video, focus is inside the iframe, so the parent document never receives the keydown. That’s why Shift+M appears broken in this specific case.
Workaround: click outside the video (or on the window chrome) before pressing Shift+M.
Memory‑leak/crash candidates tied to this flow

Duplicate windows on mode toggle: In website mode the logic can add both currentWindow and modalWindow even when they’re the same window (demo has a modal config). That can duplicate the /demo window and its player, increasing memory usage.
Source: websiteMode handling in App.tsx:2380-2392 and rendering of windows in index.tsx:45-64.
MediaPlayer cleanup is missing: MediaPlayer creates YouTube/Wistia players but never destroys/unbinds them on unmount. Re‑opening demo or toggling modes can leave player instances and iframes alive.
Source: index.tsx:41-150 (no player.destroy() / unbind in cleanup).
Duplicate /demo pages: There are two /demo routes with different implementations: demo.js and index.tsx. This can cause inconsistent behavior (iframe vs MediaPlayer), which complicates debugging and can amplify memory issues if both ever mount.

```shell
Observed behavior traced to:
- App.tsx:2048-2216
- App.tsx:2380-2392
- index.tsx:41-150

Key observations:
- document-level keydown listener loses events after iframe focus transfer
- MediaPlayer lifecycle cleanup appears missing
```

payload.body:
Users connecting to the PostHog MCP server through the claude.ai connector (including scheduled Routines) hit repeated `MCP error -32602: Tool exec not found` failures. The model attempts to call `posthog:exec(...)`, but the connection has been served tools mode, where the ~300 individual tools are registered and no `exec` dispatcher exists. In Routines this surfaces as the run failing because `exec` is not in the authorized toolset; in interactive chats the model typically retries `exec` several times before falling back to the individual tools. Users first started reporting this around May 21, 2026.

Configuring the connector via the Customize UI on claude.ai correctly shows the full list of individual tools (no `exec`), which makes the subsequent `exec` calls especially confusing from the user's perspective: the tool they are calling was never advertised to them.

## How to reproduce

1. Connect the PostHog MCP server to claude.ai via the connector / Customize UI. Confirm the tool list shows the individual tools (e.g. `execute-sql`, `query-trends`), not a single `exec` tool.
2. Create a Routine that performs a PostHog task through the connector.
3. Run the Routine. It attempts `posthog:exec(...)` and fails with `Tool exec not found`.

## Additional context

This is an upstream claude.ai bug. We have a ticket open with Anthropic, which is the next step.

### Feature request

## Problem

When analyzing funnels, users with a conversion window of X days who entered the funnel recently may not have had enough time to complete subsequent steps. This creates a downward bias in conversion rates, as those users are counted as "dropped off" when they are simply still within their conversion window.

The current workaround is to manually set a static end date shifted back by X days (equal to the conversion window). However, this is not dynamic – the insight goes stale and requires manual updates over time.

## Solution

Add a "trailing offset" option to funnel insights (and ideally to all insight types), allowing users to define a lag period relative to today. For example:
* Date range: Last 30 days
* Trailing offset: 7 days
* Effective range computed: 37 days ago → 7 days ago
This would ensure that all users included in the funnel have had at least X days to complete the conversion, producing unbiased and always up-to-date results without any manual intervention.

### Bug Description

On the project homepage, starting a PostHog AI conversation with a slash command leaves the conversation area permanently blank.

Open the "What can I help you with?" box, type `/init` (or any slash command), and press Enter. PostHog AI appears to accept it — the page title updates to *"Setting up PostHog project configurations"* and the input shows *"Thinking…"* — but the **message area stays completely blank**. You can't see the AI's questions or reply to them, so the flow is effectively stuck.

The conversation is actually running fine: open it from **Chat** in the left sidebar and the full thread is there. Only the homepage entry point is broken.

During the broken state the URL is `…/project/<id>/home?mode=ai` (no `chat=` param); the working Chat view is `…/project/<id>/ai?chat=<id>`.

<!-- Screenshots: please attach (1) the blank home?mode=ai after /init, and (2) the same thread rendering under Chat. Drag the images in here. -->

## How to reproduce

1. Go to the project homepage (`/project/<id>/home`).
2. Click the "What can I help you with?" input.
3. Type `/` (enters AI/command mode), then `init`, and press Enter — i.e. run `/init`.
4. Observe: the conversation area stays blank; input stuck on "Thinking…".
5. Open the same conversation from **Chat** in the sidebar — the full thread renders correctly.

Note: typing a normal question *without* a leading `/` and pressing Enter works fine — the thread shows. Only the `/`-trigger (slash-command) entry path is broken.

The homepage only renders the AI chat thread once an internal "thread started" flag is set. That flag is set when you submit a typed question, but **not** when you enter AI mode via the `/` trigger and then send the command — so the conversation streams into a hidden, never-mounted thread.

## Summary

PR #58697 renamed the URL path kwarg on the LLMA skills `get_by_name`/`update_by_name` endpoints from `skill_name` → `skill_identifier`. Because the MCP tool input schemas are **code-generated from these Django URL path param names**, the public required parameter for `llma-skill-get` and `llma-skill-update` silently changed from `skill_name` → `skill_identifier`. None of the docs/skills that tell agents how to call these tools were updated, so every documented call path is now wrong and fails.

cc @pauldambra (author of #58697) — flagging for discussion, not assigning blame; the rename is reasonable, it just leaked into the agent-facing contract.

## When introduced

- Commit `b7eec46cb376`, PR #58697 "fix(llma): redirect skill lookups by UUID to name-based URL"
- Merged 2026-05-26 ~07:05 UTC. **Regression is hours old, not a pre-existing edge case.**
- Prior behavior used `skill_name` (since at least the Apr 20 version of `skills.py`).

## Symptom

Calling the documented form:

```
llma-skill-get {"skill_name": "make-pr"}
```

`skill_name` is no longer a recognized parameter, so it is dropped. The request path is built with `undefined`:

```
GET /api/environments/<id>/llm_skills/name/undefined/
-> 404 {"detail": "Skill with name 'undefined' not found."}
```

The only way to call it now is `{"skill_identifier": "make-pr"}`, which no doc mentions.

## Root cause

`products/llm_analytics/backend/api/skills.py` — PR #58697 changed:

```python
- @action(methods=["GET"], detail=False, url_path=r"name/(?P<skill_name>[^/]+)")
- def get_by_name(self, request, skill_name="", **kwargs):
+ @action(methods=["GET"], detail=False, url_path=r"name/(?P<skill_identifier>[^/]+)")
+ def get_by_name(self, request, skill_identifier="", **kwargs):
```

(same for `update_by_name`). The regenerated MCP artifacts (`services/mcp/src/tools/generated/llm_analytics.ts`, `services/mcp/src/generated/llm_analytics/api.ts`, and the schema snapshots `llma-skill-get.json` / `llma-skill-update.json`) picked up the new param name, changing the public tool contract.

## Two distinct problems

**1. Doc / codegen drift (the actual break).** A required MCP param was renamed, but every place that documents the call still says `skill_name`:
- `products/llm_analytics/mcp/tools.yaml` (`llma-skill-get` / `llma-skill-update`)
- `products/llm_analytics/skills/working-with-skills/SKILL.md` — `llma-skill-get(skill_name=...)`
- `products/llm_analytics/skills/skills-store/SKILL.md` — `{ "skill_name": "make-fractals" }`
- The local `phs` / skills-store helper skills agents load

**2. Inconsistent naming across the four name-based endpoints.** Only `get_by_name`/`update_by_name` were renamed. `resolve_by_name` (skills.py ~L434) and `archive` (~L478) still use `skill_name`. So the MCP surface is now internally inconsistent:
- `llma-skill-get` / `llma-skill-update` -> `skill_identifier`
- `llma-skill-resolve` / `llma-skill-archive` -> `skill_name`

## Suggested fixes (for discussion)

- **Backwards-compatible (least churn):** revert the kwarg to `skill_name`. It already accepts a name; the new UUID->name redirect (`_is_uuid` / `_redirect_to_name`) works on the same value regardless of what the kwarg is called. No doc changes needed.
- **Keep `skill_identifier`:** then update `tools.yaml`, both SKILL.md docs, and the helper skill bodies in the same change, and rename `resolve`/`archive` for consistency.

Either way, a regression test asserting the MCP `llma-skill-get` param name (and a check that the four name-based endpoints agree) would prevent silent recurrence, since the schema is codegen'd.

## Repro

1. From any MCP client, call `llma-skill-get` with `{"skill_name": "<any existing skill>"}`.
2. Observe `404 Skill with name 'undefined' not found`.
3. Call with `{"skill_identifier": "<same skill>"}` -> works.
payload.title: MCP llma-skill-get/update param renamed skill_name -> skill_identifier (PR #58697), docs not updated -> all documented calls 404

payload.author: christiaan-ph
payload.body:
When users type using an Input Method Editor (IME), commonly used for Japanese, Chinese, Korean, and several other languages, pressing Enter to confirm a character candidate also submits the surrounding form or action. This makes a number of inputs across the PostHog UI difficult or impossible to use without switching IME off, which is impractical.

For example, typing `ue` in Japanese IME shows candidates like 上 / 飢え / 植え. Pressing Enter is supposed to confirm the highlighted candidate. Instead, the page also fires its primary action, creating the organization / sending the invite / running the query / saving the title.

A previous fix in PR #51350 addressed this in the `LemonInput` and `LemonTextArea` components, but only when consumers use the `onPressEnter` prop. Many places in the codebase wire Enter via the lower-level `onKeyDown` prop (or build on top of more primitive components), and those still hit the bug. A one-off follow-up landed for the AI-first home input in PR #60043, but the broader audit needs a single tracking issue.

## How to reproduce

1. Open one of the inputs listed below (the "Create organization" modal is a quick example)
2. Switch your OS input method to a Japanese, Chinese, or Korean IME (or any IME that uses Enter to confirm)
3. Type characters that produce candidates (for example, `ue` in Japanese)
4. Press Enter to confirm a candidate
5. Observed: the form submits, the action fires, or the highlighted suggestion is selected
6. Expected: Enter only confirms the IME candidate. Pressing Enter again on the already-confirmed (non-composing) text should then submit as normal

## Where it shows up

This is a single root cause producing many user-visible bugs. Highest impact (form-submitting / action-firing inputs):

- Creating an organization or project
- Sending team invites
- Authorizing an OAuth client
- Saving a person property
- Saving a scene, notebook, or workflow step title
- Saving an inline-edited field (used widely across the UI)
- Submitting a Lemon dialog form
- Adding an authorized domain (Conversations)
- Inserting a link in the support editor (Conversations)
- Marketing-analytics attribution settings
- Heatmaps browser URL bar
- Jump-to-timestamp form
- Screenshot annotation
- Tag inputs that add a tag on Enter (`LemonInputSelect`)

Lower impact (the wrong item gets selected, but no destructive action):

- Taxonomic filter (combobox, infinite list, autocomplete input)
- Max slash-command autocomplete
- Markdown editor inline slash commands

A grep of `e.key === 'Enter'` across `frontend/src/` and `products/*/frontend/` after filtering out a11y `key === 'Enter' || key === ' '` handlers and intentional modifier shortcuts (`metaKey + Enter`, `ctrlKey + Enter`) gives roughly 20 to 25 sites. The exact line numbers as of this writing are catalogued in the additional context section below.

## Why it happens

`LemonInput` and `LemonTextArea` define their own internal `onKeyDown` that includes the `!e.nativeEvent.isComposing` IME guard, but then spread `{...props}` immediately after, so a consumer-provided `onKeyDown` overrides the internal one. See https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/frontend/src/lib/lemon-ui/LemonInput/LemonInput.tsx#L264-L272.

This makes the guard apply only to consumers that use `onPressEnter`. Anyone using `onKeyDown` (which is allowed by the component's prop types) silently loses the guard. The same shape exists in `LemonTextArea`. Components built directly on `TextareaPrimitive`, `Autocomplete.Input`, or native inputs never had the guard at all.

## Suggested approaches

Not mutually exclusive:

1. **Per-site fix**: add `&& !e.nativeEvent.isComposing` to each Enter check across the codebase. Mechanical, easy to review, can ship incrementally.
2. **Library-level fix**: change `LemonInput` and `LemonTextArea` to wrap (not replace) the consumer's `onKeyDown` so the IME guard always applies. Needs care because the components also handle `stopPropagation` and `onP

payload.body:
## What changed

PostHog's internal scene tabs (the browser-like tab strip above the scene area) have been removed in favor of native browser tabs. See #59764 for the implementation.

## Why

Two reasons drove the removal:

1. **Restoring per-tab state is a huge undertaking.** Users reasonably expected that switching back to a tab would put them exactly where they left it: every input value, every scroll position, every bit of in-memory state. Doing that well across an app this size requires persisting and rehydrating state for every scene, on every tab switch, while staying within our memory budget. We have ongoing work to reduce frontend memory pressure, and competing investment in tab-state persistence pulled against it.
2. **Tabs overrode normal browser behavior.** The right-click menu on links was replaced with a custom one, and links with `target="_blank"` opened as scene tabs instead of real browser tabs. Both of those make the app inconsistent with what users expect from the web platform, and we'd rather hand those behaviors back to the browser than ship a subpar imitation.

We'd rather do one thing well (rely on real browser tabs) than ship a partial version of something browsers already nail.

## Usage data at the time of removal (PostHog App + Website)

Most opens came from in-app navigation rather than the explicit new-tab button, and "opened" outpaced "closed" by roughly 2.7×, suggesting most users left tabs open rather than actively curating them.

## What you can still do

- **Open a page in a new browser tab**: Cmd/Ctrl-click any link, or right-click and choose "Open in new tab".
- **Pin frequently used pages**: pin them as browser tabs in Chrome, Firefox, Safari, or Arc.
- **Reopen a closed tab**: Cmd/Ctrl-Shift-T.

## Want to weigh in?

Use this issue to share:

- What you used scene tabs for that's harder now.
- Whether browser tabs cover your workflow.
- Workflows where you think we should reconsider.
- Anything else you'd like to share.

We're keeping this issue open as the canonical place for feedback on the change. We may not bring the feature back, but specific friction reports will inform what we build next (e.g., another form of organization of links, better deep links, pinnable home tiles, faster scene navigation).

## Reference

- Implementation PR: #59764
- Modal users see on first load after the change: `frontend/src/layout/scenes/GoodbyeTabsModal.tsx`
payload.title: [Discussion] Removal of PostHog tabs

payload.body:
### Feature request

## Is your feature request related to a problem?

Yes. I use PostHog Sources extensively to bring data from external systems and then create SQL views to analyze users in my product.

When I create a view, I intentionally define the columns in an order that makes sense for analysis and readability. However, when I later run:

SELECT * FROM my_view

the returned columns appear in a seemingly random order, instead of following the order I used when creating the view.

This makes the output harder to read and analyze, especially when the view has many columns or when I am using the result in saved queries, dashboards, or repeated analysis workflows.

## Describe the solution you'd like

I would like PostHog to preserve the column order defined in the SQL view.

For example, if I create a view like:

SELECT
    user_id,
    email,
    signup_date,
    plan,
    last_seen_at
FROM source_table

then running:

SELECT * FROM my_view

should return the columns in that same order:

user_id, email, signup_date, plan, last_seen_at

This would make views more predictable and easier to work with.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

The current workaround is to avoid `SELECT *` and manually specify the columns in every query, in the exact order I want.

That works, but it defeats part of the purpose of creating reusable views. It also adds extra maintenance whenever the view changes, because every downstream query needs to be updated manually.

## Additional context

This is especially useful for users who build analytical datasets using Sources and SQL views, where column order is part of the way the dataset is organized and understood.

Preserving the view’s column order would make the behavior more intuitive and consistent with what users expect when querying a structured view.


payload.author: matheus-vb
payload.body:
## Problem

The Rust feature-flags service classifies bot traffic against two hardcoded tables in `rust/feature-flags/src/utils/bot_detection.rs`: `BOT_PATTERNS` (mirrors the posthog-js `DEFAULT_BLOCKED_UA_STRS` list) and `BOT_CIDRS` (Googlebot, Bingbot, YandexBot, and Applebot supernets pulled from each provider's JSON file). Both drift. Google publishes new IP ranges every few weeks, and the SDK list grows as new bots appear, but nothing in this repo notices.

## Proposed approach

Mimic the GeoLite pattern at `bin/download-mmdb`. Add a script that fetches the four provider IP feeds and the SDK pattern list, writes them under `share/`, and stamps a sibling JSON with the fetch date. The feature-flags service loads the tables from `share/` at startup instead of compiling them in. CI fails when the on-disk copy is missing or older than a configurable threshold.

## Acceptance

The bot tables refresh on a known cadence. The build fails closed when the data is stale or missing. The Rust loader keeps its current `LazyLock` shape so the hot path stays allocation-free.

### Feature request

## Is your feature request related to a problem?

The recent PR #58224 successfully isolated and preserved ephemeral UI state (like Max chat drafts and DataTable filters) across internal tab switches by introducing `tabUiStateLogic`. However, because this logic is currently kept in-memory, users still lose their active workspace context upon a hard page refresh or a browser restart.

It breaks the flow when picking up work the next day. This is a UX / UI fix.

## Describe the solution you'd like

Extend `tabUiStateLogic` to persist its state to `localStorage`, wrapped in a TTL mechanism that refreshes on use, so the state survives restarts for active users, but doesn't haunt people returning months later.

**Proposed implementation:**
1. **Storage:** Single `localStorage` key (`ph_tab_ui_state`) holding the serialized state blob. No per-tab keys –reading and writing a single unified blob keeps things simple and avoids partial-write races.
2. **Payload shape:** `{ version: 1, updatedAt: <timestamp>, state: {...} }`.
3. **TTL:** 30 days, refreshed on every write. The `updatedAt` timestamp is rewritten whenever state changes (including the initial hydrate-then-write on load), so the clock resets as long as the user keeps using the app. Idle for 30 days → clean state on next visit.
4. **Lazy expire on read:** No useless background cron. If `now - updatedAt > TTL` at read time, ignore the payload and start fresh. The next write overwrites it.
5. **Schema versioning:** The `version` field lets us safely evolve the state shape later – bump the version and treat older payloads as expired.
6. **Quota guard:** Wrap writes in `try/catch`. On `QuotaExceededError`, swallow + capture using console.warn (don't crash the UI, noninvasive). The payload is small (kB-range), but PostHog already shares `localStorage` with `kea-localstorage`, `posthog-js`, and feature flag caches.
7. **Hydration:** Synchronous read inside `kea` defaults so the first render sees the restored state – no flicker from an empty initial state followed by an `afterMount` rehydrate.

**Open questions / non-goals for this PR:**
* **Per-user namespacing** (`ph_tab_ui_state__${userId}`): Intentional skipped. Shared workstations get the previous user's layout on login, but nothing sensitive is stored (just which tabs were open). Adding it complicates hydration because `userId` must be resolved before the first read. Open to revisiting if it causes confusion in practice.
* **Cross-tab sharing:** Two PostHog browser tabs share the same key. Last write wins, both converge, which is acceptable imo, but worth mentioninng.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

* **`sessionStorage`:** Survives hard refreshes but drops on browser close; this doesn't solve the "pick up where I left off tomorrow" use-case = poor UX.
* **`localStorage` without TTL:** Unbounded staleness. Six month old tab references to deleted insights are worse than a clean start.
* **URL hash / query param:** 2nd best option for per-scene layout state and shareable via link, but a poor fit for "list of open internal tabs". It pollutes the URL and collides with existing scene-level hash usage (eg. when you share with your colleague / anybody else).
* **Keeping it ephemeral (current state):** Safe, but frustrating after an accidental `Cmd+R`, device crash...

## Additional context

Direct follow-up / phase 2 to the tab UI state persistence effort, as discussed with @mariusandra in PR #58224.

Happy to draft this up if the TTL + versioning + lazy-expire architecture sounds good.

# Context

**We are working towards becoming an AI-first company**. For us to be seen as such, we need to start _blurring the lines between each product we have_. We go from different products to different tools one might use to solve a problem. ### Feature request

## Is your feature request related to a problem?

Some Google Cloud products (e.g. Cloud Load Balancing) produce logs that live inside Google Cloud Logging and are not emitted by application code. These logs can't be instrumented with an OTLP library because they originate from Google's own infrastructure, not from a user-controlled process. The only way to export them is via Google Cloud's log router, which can sync logs to Pub/Sub topics, Cloud Storage buckets, BigQuery, or Splunk, but not to an arbitrary OTLP HTTP endpoint like PostHog's.

Users who rely on load balancer logs for reliability and latency evaluation (as the closest-to-user signal they fully control) currently can't get those logs into PostHog without deploying and maintaining a middleman service (e.g. an OpenTelemetry Collector with a Pub/Sub receiver, or a Cloud Function that reads from a bucket and POSTs to PostHog's OTLP endpoint).

## Describe the solution you'd like

A native integration that can pull logs from Google Cloud log router syncs. The most flexible options would be:

1. **Pub/Sub subscription**: PostHog subscribes to (or pulls from) a Google Cloud Pub/Sub topic that receives logs via a log router sync.
2. **Cloud Storage reader**: PostHog periodically reads log files from a GCS bucket that receives logs via a log router sync.

Either approach would let users route any Google Cloud infrastructure logs into PostHog without maintaining extra infrastructure.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

- **OTel Collector as middleman**: Deploy an OpenTelemetry Collector with the `googlecloudpubsub` receiver and an OTLP HTTP exporter pointed at PostHog. Works but adds infrastructure to manage.
- **Cloud Function/Cloud Run**: Write a small service that subscribes to Pub/Sub and POSTs to PostHog's OTLP endpoint. Same operational overhead concern.
- **Datadog Agent as middleman**: Since PostHog has a Datadog-compatible log endpoint, one could theoretically route through a Datadog Agent, but this is even more complicated.

## Additional context
From: https://posthoghelp.zendesk.com/agent/tickets/51220 (moved to PostHog: https://us.posthog.com/project/2/support/tickets/60009)

PostHog AI sometimes presents an insight it has just generated as if it can be opened from a URL, when in reality the insight is a transient artifact scoped to the conversation. The agent produces a markdown link of the form `[Insight title (<id>)](/insights/<id>)` in its reply, where `<id>` is the in-conversation artifact id and is not a real saved-insight short_id. ## How to reproduce

1. Open PostHog AI in any project (default mode is fine).
2. Ask the agent to build any chart, e.g. "show me average X by day of week as a bar chart".
3. In a follow-up turn, ask the agent for a link to the insight, or for the SQL.

payload.author: andrewm4894
payload.body:
## Question for the team

Cross-posting from an internal Slack thread so this doesn't get lost. Wiring this up as a question rather than a bug since the omission may be deliberate — flagging the spot in code that surprised me, but happy to be told "yeah, that's on purpose, here's why."

## What I observed

When connecting the Slack data warehouse source (alpha, behind `slack-dwh` flag) and picking a channel schema, the UI only offers **Full refresh** as the sync type. Incremental and Append are not selectable.

For a high-volume channel this means we re-pull the entire channel from `conversations.history` every sync interval, which is expensive (Tier-2 limits) and predictably gets close to the rate-limit storm class of issue that #57567 (draft) is trying to fix.

## Where it seems to come from

`posthog/temporal/data_imports/sources/slack/settings.py:24-30`:

```python
def messages_endpoint_config() -> EndpointConfig:
    return EndpointConfig(
        primary_keys=["channel_id", "ts"],
        partition_keys=["timestamp"],
        partition_mode="datetime",
        partition_format="week",
    )
```

No ` incremental_fields=...` is passed, so it defaults to `[]` (`EndpointConfig` definition at `settings.py:9-15`).

The UI capabilities for each channel schema are derived directly from that in `source.py:200-205`:

```python
supports_incremental=len(msg_config.incremental_fields) > 0,  # False
supports_webhooks=webhook_flag_enabled,
supports_append=len(msg_config.incremental_fields) > 0,        # False
```

So with `incremental_fields=[]`, the schema advertises neither incremental nor append, and the UI hides both options.

## What's interesting

The runtime path already handles incremental for channel messages. In `slack.py:433-439`:

```python
oldest_ts: str | None = None
if should_use_incremental_field and db_incremental_field_last_value is not None:
    # Known limitation: incremental polling only fetches thread replies for parent messages
    # returned by conversations.history in this window. Replies added to older parent threads
    # (parent ts < oldest_ts) are intentionally not captured here and are expected to be
    # addressed by webhook sources.
    oldest_ts = str(db_incremental_field_last_value.timestamp())
```

That branch reads the last `timestamp` value and passes it to Slack's `oldest` parameter on `conversations.history`. So the engine is already wired up — only the schema declaration is missing the `incremental_fields` entry that the UI keys off of.

The `timestamp` column itself looks stable enough to be an incremental field — it's derived from Slack's message `ts` (microsecond unix timestamp) in `_add_timestamp()` (`slack.py:303-307`), and `ts` is part of the primary key, so it's monotonic per channel for new messages.

## Question

Is this:

1. **An oversight** — `incremental_fields` should be declared on `messages_endpoint_config()` and we should expose Incremental / Append in the UI?
2. **Deliberate** — there's a known reason (the thread-replies gap noted in the comment, partition format being weekly, something about how `ts` behaves under workspace clock skew or edits, etc.) that the team wants to address with the webhook source instead of incremental polling?
3. **Pending** — incremental on channels is on the roadmap and just hasn't landed?

If (1), I'm happy to PR the change — would look roughly like:

```python
def messages_endpoint_config() -> EndpointConfig:
    return EndpointConfig(
        primary_keys=["channel_id", "ts"],
        partition_keys=["timestamp"],
        partition_mode="datetime",
        partition_format="week",
        incremental_fields=[
            IncrementalField(
                label="timestamp",
                type=IncrementalFieldType.DateTime,
                field="timestamp",
                field_type=IncrementalFieldType.DateTime,
            ),
        ],
    )
```

Plus a test that asserts channel schemas come back with `supports_incremental=True`.

## Is your feature request related to a problem?

When viewing the results of an LLM evaluation, users can only see aggregate metrics (pass rate, runs count, failing count) across all matching `$ai_generation` events. There is no way to slice those results by an event property such as `$ai_environment`, a prompt version property, or any other custom dimension. This makes it hard to compare evaluation outcomes across environments (e.g. staging vs production) or across prompt variants in an A/B test, which are two common workflows for users iterating on LLM features.

## Describe the solution you'd like

Add a "breakdown" option to the evaluation results view that takes any event property and renders a per-value breakdown of the existing summary cards, pass-rate trend chart, and runs table. A user looking at an evaluation should be able to pick `$ai_environment` (or any other property they capture) and see a side-by-side comparison of pass rate, run count, and failing count for each value of that property, without having to duplicate the evaluation. The breakdown should apply to both the trend chart and the summary, so users can compare environments at a glance and drill into the runs for each segment.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

**- Writing raw HogQL or Creating custom insights and dashboards against `$ai_evaluation` events. Gives full flexibility but bypasses the evaluation UX entirely. (currently the best workaround)**
- Duplicating the evaluation and adding a property filter for each dimension. This is the current workaround. Works, but doubles LLM judge spend on overlapping generations, scales poorly when there are more than two values to compare, and leaves stale duplicates behind whenever the underlying eval prompt or config changes.
- Clicking the "Trend insight" button on the evaluation detail page, which opens a Trends insight pre-filtered to the evaluation. Native Trends breakdowns work there, but the user loses the summary cards, runs table, and AI patterns view, and the breakdown is not persisted with the evaluation.


## Additional context

Customer feedback: would love to be able to break down by dimension when viewing LLM evaluation results. Two specific use cases called out:

1. Running evals in staging (or any non-prod environment) and comparing pass rates against production before promoting a change.
2. A/B testing prompts and comparing metrics between prompt variants.

Raised in: [posthoghelp.zendesk.com/agent/tickets/58462](https://posthoghelp.zendesk.com/agent/tickets/58462) (moved to PostHog: https://us.posthog.com/project/2/support/tickets/59373)

## Is your feature request related to a problem?

PostHog AI users encounter rough edges (missing features, unexpected behavior, etc.) during conversations with the assistant but have no in-flow way to capture them as a GitHub issue. Today the only path is to navigate to the Share feedback panel and open the GitHub feature request form manually, which loses the conversation context that made the issue obvious in the first place.

## Describe the solution you'd like

Add a PostHog AI tool that drafts a feature-request or bug-report body from the current conversation context, then opens a pre-filled github.com/PostHog/posthog/issues/new URL the user can review and submit. The tool should not file issues directly via the GitHub API in a first version, to avoid spam and abuse concerns: the user submitting under their own GitHub identity is the right access control.

Important nuance: PostHog AI often categorizes normal product behavior as "bugs". The tool prompt and UX should bias toward feature requests and confirm with the user before producing a body, so it doesn't turn into a noise source for the team.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

The existing Share feedback side panel already links to the GitHub feature request URL but doesn't carry over conversation context: https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/frontend/src/layout/navigation-3000/sidepanel/panels/support/SidePanelSupport.tsx

A more ambitious API-submitting tool was considered but rejected for v1 due to spam and abuse concerns.

## Is your feature request related to a problem?

Customers using a SQL or HogQL insight to plot data bucketed by a date property (e.g. `delivery_date` set on the event payload, then `GROUP BY toStartOfDay(properties.delivery_date)`) cannot use annotations to mark significant moments on the chart. SQL/HogQL insights currently don't render annotations at all: `AnnotationsOverlay` is only used by the Trends `LineGraph` component, not by the `DataVisualization` charts used for SQL/HogQL insights.

This is felt acutely when the customer's analytical workflow inherently uses a property date (delivery date, order date, signup cohort date) rather than the event ingestion timestamp.

## Describe the solution you'd like

Two parts:

1. Render annotations on SQL/HogQL date-axis insights (DataVisualization line/bar charts). Today they're only rendered on Trends `LineGraph`.
2. When the X-axis is a date property (not `events.timestamp`), annotations should align with the property values rather than ingestion time. This likely means matching annotation `date_marker` against the X-axis date values produced by the SQL query, not against the timestamp-derived buckets currently used.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

- Adding the date logic into the SQL query as a separate series so the markers are visible inline. Workable but defeats the point of having annotations as first-class.
- Using the SDK `timestamp` parameter to backdate events to the property date. Possible only if every event has a one-to-one mapping with the property; not realistic when the property is set or updated after ingestion, or when the same event has multiple meaningful dates.

## Additional context

Relevant code:
- `AnnotationsOverlay` is invoked from Trends `LineGraph` only: https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/frontend/src/scenes/insights/views/LineGraph/LineGraph.tsx#L1310
- No usage of `AnnotationsOverlay` anywhere under `frontend/src/queries/` (the home of SQL/HogQL DataVisualization)
- `Annotation.date_marker` is a single DateTimeField: https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/posthog/models/annotation.py
- Trends overlay logic positions annotations by matching `date_marker` against the chart's `dates[]` array: https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/frontend/src/lib/components/AnnotationsOverlay/annotationsOverlayLogic.ts
