Context/ Problem:

PostHog currently labels the first day in retention cohort charts as D0, with subsequent days as D1, D2, etc. Many teams (including ours) use a different convention where the first event day is called D1, and the next day is D2. This mismatch creates ongoing confusion when sharing charts with stakeholders, since our "D2 retention" target (return within 24h of first deposit) appears as the "D1" column in PostHog. Team members constantly need to mentally shift all numbers when reading or presenting charts. We currently have no workaround. Renaming in downstream tools (e.g., Looker Studio) is possible but adds friction and breaks the connection to PostHog's native chart. This is a common convention difference between analytics tools and business/product KPI reporting. A configurable starting index would make PostHog charts easier to use for teams whose reporting language starts at D1.

Suggested solution:

An option in the retention chart settings to configure the starting day label, specifically, the ability to start from D1 instead of D0. This could be a simple toggle or a numeric input for "starting day index."

## Bug Description

Installing the Supabase MCP server template from the MCP Store fails during OAuth authorization. The browser redirects to Supabase with a `client_id` that Supabase rejects as unrecognized.

## How to reproduce

1. Open PostHog Code
2. Go to MCP Servers / MCP Store
3. Click install on the Supabase template
4. Browser opens:
   ```
   https://api.supabase.com/v1/oauth/authorize?client_id=18038368-50b4-4095-a1b6-b67b73417452&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fus.posthog.com%2Fapi%2Fmcp_store%2Foauth_redirect%2F&response_type=code&...
   ```
5. Supabase returns: `{"message": "Unrecognized client_id"}`

## Expected behavior

OAuth flow should complete successfully and the Supabase MCP server should be installed and connected.

## Actual behavior

The `client_id` embedded in the authorization URL is rejected by Supabase. This means the OAuth app credentials stored in the Supabase template (`MCPServerTemplate.oauth_credentials` on the PostHog backend) are either stale, incorrect, or the app was never properly registered on Supabase's side.

## Environment

- **PostHog Code**: v0.52.9 (commit 890696c)
- **Platform**: Linux x86_64
- **PostHog region**: US (`us.posthog.com`)

## Pointers

The OAuth flow for template-based installs is handled in:
- `apps/code/src/renderer/features/mcp-servers/hooks/useMcpServers.ts` — `installTemplateWithOAuth()`
- `apps/code/src/renderer/api/posthogClient.ts` — `installTemplateWithOAuth()` API call
- Backend template model: `products/mcp_store/backend/models.py` in `PostHog/posthog` — `MCPServerTemplate.oauth_credentials`

The fix likely requires updating the `client_id`/`client_secret` in the Supabase template record via Django admin on the PostHog backend, or re-registering the OAuth app on Supabase.
payload.title: MCP Store: Supabase template OAuth fails with "Unrecognized client_id"

payload.author: gantoine
payload.body:
## Context

PR #59070 wires `@typescript/native-preview` (tsgo) as a shadow type-checker alongside `tsc`, with `typescript@6.0.3` retained via `pnpm.overrides` for every tool that consumes the programmatic Compiler API. The largest such consumer is **kea-typegen**, which generates the `*Type.ts` files we depend on for kea logic typing.

This issue tracks the upstream gaps that block migrating kea-typegen (and the rest of our programmatic-API consumers) off `typescript@6`.

## Why this is blocked today

`@typescript/native-preview` currently ships **zero JS-callable code** — `package.json` has no `main`/`types`, only a `bin` entry that subprocesses the native binary. The "Corsa" IPC API exists in [microsoft/typescript-go](https://github.com/microsoft/typescript-go) source (`_packages/native-preview/src/api/sync/api.ts`) but is not bundled to npm.

Even once Corsa ships, kea-typegen's hot path needs APIs that aren't designed yet:

- `ts.factory.*` — kea-typegen **constructs** `*Type.ts` AST nodes
- `ts.createPrinter` — serializes constructed nodes to text
- `checker.typeToTypeNode` — converts a resolved `Type` back into a printable `TypeNode`
- `checker.typeToString`, `checker.getExportsOfModule` — listed as gaps, no open PR

There is also an architectural mismatch: kea-typegen holds live `ts.Node` references across many checker calls and mutates the AST in-memory. Corsa is IPC: opaque handles, serialize/deserialize per call. No in-process AST graph.

## Upstream issues to watch

- microsoft/TypeScript#63771 — _Transformer Plugin or Compiler API_ (open, no timeline)
- microsoft/TypeScript#63800 — _API usage patterns for complex editor extensions_ (Corsa design)
- microsoft/typescript-go#3610 — _API: additional Checker methods for transpiler consumers_ (subset of methods landing incrementally; `typeToTypeNode` is a listed gap)
- microsoft/typescript-go#3616 — _API emit support_ (open PR, not merged)

## Definition of done

- [ ] `@typescript/native-preview` (or a Microsoft-blessed sibling package) ships a JS-importable module with: `ts.factory`, `ts.createPrinter`, `ts.createSourceFile`, `Program.getTypeChecker()`, `TypeChecker.typeToTypeNode`, `TypeChecker.typeToString`, `TypeChecker.getExportsOfModule`, and the ~40 `ts.is*` AST predicates kea-typegen relies on.
- [ ] kea-typegen's `peerDependencies.typescript` is bumped to support the 7.x line.
- [ ] We drop the `pnpm.overrides.typescript = "6.0.3"` pin and rely on the catalog entry only.
- [ ] Same applies to other API consumers we currently pin: `ts-jest`, `ts-node`, `ts-json-schema-generator`, `@parcel/packager-ts`, `@parcel/transformer-typescript-types`.

## Realistic timeline

TS 7.1 at the earliest, more likely 7.2+. Microsoft has not committed to a date. No engineering action is feasible until upstream lands the APIs above — this is a watch-list, not a backlog item.

## Related

- PR #59070 — adds the tsgo shadow CI step and the coexistence setup this issue depends on.
payload.title: Track upstream TypeScript 7 (tsgo) APIs needed for kea-typegen migration

payload.author: andrewm4894
payload.body:
## Is your feature request related to a problem?

The skills store currently has no metadata for categorizing or tagging skills. Most existing skills are designed for interactive use — you invoke them when you're in the middle of a task and want guidance. But there's a growing use case for automation: agent runs triggered on a schedule (e.g. via PostHog Code). Without a way to distinguish "interactive" skills from skills suitable for scheduled/autonomous runs, it's hard to build UIs or workflows that surface only the relevant ones for automation.

## Describe the solution you'd like

Some form of structured metadata on skills — at minimum a notion of category/tag so we can mark skills as suitable for automation vs. interactive-only. This would let downstream features (like PostHog Code's scheduled agent runs) filter the skills store to just the relevant subset when configuring a cron-triggered agent.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

- Naming conventions in skill titles/descriptions (fragile, not enforced)
- A separate store for "automation skills" (duplicates infrastructure)
- Filtering by skill content heuristics (unreliable)

## Additional context

Came up in a thread with Olly, who's happy to drive the implementation but wanted to double-check nothing is already planned and that the direction is sound. Andy mentioned Radu had flagged metadata as a likely next iteration for the skills store, so this issue is to track it explicitly.

Primary motivating use case: configuring scheduled agent runs in PostHog Code that pick a skill to execute autonomously.
payload.title: Feature request: categorize/tag skills in the skills store

payload.author: darkopia
payload.body:
### Feature request

Currently, PostHog experiments only support upper/lower bound percentile filtering for outlier management across all exposed users. This creates issues when analyzing metrics for features with low adoption rates.

For example, with 10,000 exposures per variant but only 80-50 users actually using the feature, setting percentile bounds at 99% filters out the actual feature users rather than just outliers. This makes it impossible to get meaningful percentile metrics (P50/P75/P90) for the subset of users who engaged with the feature.

Describe the solution you'd like
Add support for percentile metrics (P50, P75, P90, P95, P99) in experiment results that can be calculated specifically for users who performed the target action, rather than across all exposed users.

This would allow filtering outliers within the engaged user subset, providing more accurate statistical analysis for features with low conversion rates.

Describe alternatives you've considered
Currently using upper/lower bound percentiles at 99.9%, but this doesn't solve the core issue when feature usage is very low relative to total exposures.

Manual HogQL queries could potentially calculate these metrics, but this requires significant technical overhead and doesn't integrate with the experiment UI.

Additional context
This is particularly important for experiments testing new features or UI changes where only a small percentage of exposed users actually interact with the changed element. The customer has experienced this across multiple experiments with uneven traffic splits (80/20) where outlier management becomes critical for accurate results.

payload.author: praneya0028
payload.body:
## Bug description

Follow-up to #58656 / #58658. The "Leave feature flag? Changes you made will be discarded." dialog can prompt **twice** in a row when the user clicks Cancel. Cancel-still-discards is fixed by #58658; this issue tracks the remaining double-prompt half.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open any feature flag edit page (`/feature_flags/<id>`).
2. Edit any field (key, name, payload, rollout %).
3. Trigger a navigation that fires `beforeUnload` (browser tab switch, sidebar link).
4. Click **Cancel** on the "Leave feature flag?" dialog.

**Expected:** Dialog dismissed, stay on the page.
**Actual:** The same dialog appears again, requiring a second Cancel click before it stays dismissed.

(After #58658 merges, the form data is preserved — but the double prompt UX bug remains.)

## Suspected root cause

The new `beforeUnload` block added by #54692 in `frontend/src/scenes/feature-flags/featureFlagLogic.ts` (around the block flagged by `TODO` comment) lacks the **scene-tab-cache guard** that `products/actions/frontend/logics/actionEditLogic.tsx` (L305-332) uses for the same scenario.

In `actionEditLogic.tsx` the `beforeUnload.enabled` callback explicitly checks `sceneLogic` `activeTabId` vs the logic's own `props.tabId` and returns `false` for tab switches, with a comment noting *"the logic stays mounted via the scene-logic cache"*. `featureFlagLogic` has no equivalent guard — it also doesn't import `sceneLogic`, `FeatureFlagLogicProps` has no `tabId`, and `key()` is keyed only by `id`. When the logic stays mounted in a cached background scene tab, both instances participate in routing and the prompt fires twice.

## Suggested fix

Apply the `/making-scenes-tab-aware` skill to the feature-flags scene:

1. Add `tabId?: string` to `FeatureFlagLogicProps`.
2. Update `key()` to include `tabId` (mirror `actionEditLogic.tsx` L52).
3. Update the `SceneExport`'s `paramsToProps` in `FeatureFlag.tsx` to pass `tabId`.
4. Port the tab-id / scene-cache guard from `actionEditLogic.tsx` L305-332 into the `beforeUnload.enabled` callback in `featureFlagLogic.ts`.
5. Add the `logic.isMounted()` check the same callback in `actionEditLogic.tsx` uses.
6. Add a regression test in `featureFlagLogic.test.ts` covering the cached-background-tab path.

## Scope

This is intentionally split out of #58658 because it touches the scene mount, props shape, and `key()` — wider blast radius than the small `urlToAction` guard #58658 ships. Filing separately so each PR stays cleanly reviewable.

Happy to take this in a follow-up PR after #58658 merges.
payload.title: Bug: "Leave feature flag?" dialog prompts twice on Cancel (scene-tab-cache guard missing)

payload.body:
## Feature request: Dynamic UNION ALL across PostgreSQL schemas

### Is your feature request related to a problem?
Yes

**Problem:**
Currently, to query the same table across multiple PostgreSQL schemas (e.g., `order_order` table in 900+ client schemas), users must manually write hundreds of UNION ALL statements:

```sql
SELECT * FROM postgres.schema1.order_order
UNION ALL
SELECT * FROM postgres.schema2.order_order
UNION ALL
-- ... 900+ more lines
```

This is impractical for users with multi-schema databases (one schema per client).

### Describe the solution you'd like
**Dynamic UNION feature:**

1. User selects a table (e.g., `order_order`)
2. Choose target schemas: "all schemas" or "specific schemas" 
3. System automatically generates UNION ALL query across all selected schemas
4. User can save result as a view

**Example:**
- Input: Select table `order_order`, choose "all schemas"
- Output: Auto-generated query pulling from all 900+ schemas' `order_order` tables

### Describe alternatives you've considered
Manual UNION ALL (current workaround - not scalable)

### Additional context
Related to issue #58643 - Multi-Schema Postgres DB  
This would complement the "Include all schemas" / "Specific schemas" feature in PR #58694

## Status: IMPLEMENTED ✅
This feature has been implemented in PR #58694!

**Usage:**
1. Navigate to your PostgreSQL data source in PostHog
2. Click on the "Generate UNION Query" action
3. Optionally specify a table name and schemas to filter
4. The API returns a UNION ALL query that you can use in the SQL editor

Example API call:
```
GET /api/projects/{project_id}/external_data_sources/{source_id}/generate_union_query?table_name=order_order&schemas=schema1&schemas=schema2
```

**Labels:** enhancement, data-warehouse, postgres
payload.title: Feature request: Dynamic UNION ALL across PostgreSQL schemas (IMPLEMENTED)

### Feature request

Is your feature request related to a problem?

When running experiments, there's no native way to use "average time between two events" as a metric. Users who want to measure things like time-to-complete a task, time between activation steps, or time from first action to conversion have to resort to workarounds. This makes it hard to use time-based metrics as experiment success criteria without extra instrumentation.

Describe the solution you'd like

A new experiment metric type (or an extension of the existing Mean metric) that allows users to select two events – a start event and an end event – and automatically computes the average time elapsed between them per user, then compares that mean across variants statistically.

This would mirror the "average time to convert" already shown in funnel insights, but exposed as a proper experiment metric with statistical significance testing.

Describe alternatives you've considered

Custom property on end event: Calculate the time delta client-side and send it as a property (e.g. time_to_complete_ms), then use a Mean metric on that property. This works but requires extra instrumentation and isn't available for users who don't control the event schema.
Funnel metric: Funnels show average/median conversion time between steps, but this isn't surfaced as a comparable numeric metric in experiments.

- `POST   /api/projects/<pid>/hog_flows/user_blast_radius/`
- `POST   /api/projects/<pid>/hog_flows/bulk_delete/`

Base CRUD (`list`, `retrieve`, `create`, `update`, `partial_update`, `destroy`) plus the explicitly declared read actions (`logs`, `metrics`, `metrics_totals`) work as expected with a personal API key holding `hog_flow:write` scope.

Same response on `/api/environments/...` mirror paths — both URL prefixes route to the same viewset and trip the same permission check. The same auth path succeeds via session cookie (the path the PostHog UI uses), so the data layer and serializers are not the issue.

## Reproduction

Personal API key with `hog_flow:read` and `hog_flow:write` scopes on EU Cloud:

```bash
curl -sX GET \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer phx_REDACTED" \
  "https://eu.posthog.com/api/projects/<pid>/hog_flows/<flow_id>/schedules/"
```

Response (HTTP 403):

```json
{
  "type": "authentication_error",
  "code": "permission_denied",
  "detail": "This action does not support personal API key access",
  "attr": null
}
```

Same 403 on every endpoint listed above. Same response on `/api/environments/...` paths. CRUD on the parent `/hog_flows/` resource works fine with the same key.

**Retested with an all-access personal API key** (every scope granted, no restrictions): identical 403. Confirms the rejection is not scope-shortage — `_get_required_scopes` returns `None` before scope evaluation runs, so no token (regardless of scopes) can pass.

## Root cause

`HogFlowViewSet` (`posthog/api/hog_flow.py:436-439`) declares:

```python
class HogFlowViewSet(TeamAndOrgViewSetMixin, LogEntryMixin, AppMetricsMixin, viewsets.ModelViewSet):
    scope_object = "hog_flow"
    scope_object_read_actions = ["list", "retrieve", "logs", "metrics", "metrics_totals"]
    queryset = HogFlow.objects.all()
    ...
```

There is no `scope_object_write_actions` attribute. The permission layer at `posthog/permissions.py:434-461`:

```python
def _get_required_scopes(self, request, view) -> Optional[list[str]]:
    ...
    action = self._get_action(request, view)
    read_actions = getattr(view, "scope_object_read_actions", self.read_actions)
    write_actions = getattr(view, "scope_object_write_actions", self.write_actions)

    if action in write_actions:
        return [f"{scope_object}:write"]
    elif action in read_actions or request.method == "OPTIONS":
        return [f"{scope_object}:read"]

    return None
```

Custom `@action` methods like `schedules`, `batch_jobs`, `user_blast_radius`, `invocations`, `bulk_delete` are not in either list. `getattr` falls back to the base `write_actions = ["create", "update", "partial_update", "patch", "destroy"]` from `ScopeBasePermission` (`posthog/permissions.py:416`), which doesn't include the custom action names. `_get_required_scopes` returns `None`, which triggers:

```python
if not required_scopes:
    self.message = "This action does not support personal API key access"
    return False
```

at `posthog/permissions.py:497-499`.

## Comparison with sibling viewset (already correct)

`HogFunctionViewSet` (`posthog/api/hog_function.py:478`) declares both lists:

```python
scope_object = "hog_function"
scope_object_read_actions = ["list", "retrieve", "logs", "metrics", "metrics_totals"]
scope_object_write_actions = ["create", "update", "part
payload.title: Bug: HogFlowViewSet custom actions reject all personal API key access

payload.author: christiaan-ph
payload.body:
## Bug Description

When a user asks PostHog AI a complex question with a large dashboard attached as context, the agent can fail silently with no response shown in the chat.

The Temporal activity that runs the chat agent has a 5 minute (300 s) heartbeat timeout, and heartbeats are only emitted when the LangGraph stream yields a chunk. If the root node runs for longer than 300 s without yielding anything, no heartbeat fires and Temporal cancels the activity with asyncio.CancelledError at ~300 s. No FailureMessage is yielded. The user sees no response and no error.

This is amplified by the activity's retry policy (maximum_attempts=3). Each retry replays from the checkpointer, so the input state grows on every attempt. In one observed trace the state grew from ~95 KB to ~285 KB across three retries, all of which were cancelled at exactly 309 s. In a separate trace from the same user the first attempt was cancelled the same way but a later retry succeeded, so the failure is intermittent. (links to traces in ticket below)

## How to reproduce

1. Open PostHog AI in a project that has at least one moderately large dashboard (around 20+ insights).
2. Attach the dashboard as context and send a multi-part analytical question (several distinct asks combined into one prompt) in the default product_analytics agent mode.
3. Wait. After about 5 minutes the agent will be silently cancelled, with no reply or error shown in the chat.

## Additional context

Raised in: https://posthoghelp.zendesk.com/agent/tickets/58027 (moved to PostHog: https://us.posthog.com/project/2/support/tickets/59923)

I might raise a PR just to stop the silent failure as well, will attach here once it's done.
payload.title: Bug(PostHog AI): chat / PostHog AI doesn't respond to message, doesn't show an error

### Feature request

Is your feature request related to a problem?
PostHog displays person names (e.g. "First Last") across many surfaces – session replay list, person profiles, funnel breakdowns, activity logs, cohorts, and more. For B2B products, a person's name alone is rarely enough context. You need to know which business they belong to to make sense of the data. There is currently no way to configure a display format that includes company or group properties alongside the person's name.

Describe the solution you'd like
A project-level setting to configure a person display name template using person or group properties. For example:

Template: {firstName} {lastName} ({businessName})
Result: "Mo Khalil (Bella Booking)"
This should apply consistently everywhere a person's name is shown:

Session replay list
Person profiles and person modal
Funnel breakdowns
Cohort member lists
Activity logs
Any other surface that displays a person's identity
Describe alternatives you've considered
Setting $name to a composite string like "First Last (Business Name)" during posthog.identify() works as a workaround, but it pollutes the $name property globally, makes it harder to use name independently, and requires re-identifying users if the business name changes.

Additional context
This is a fundamental B2B product analytics need. When your users are employees of businesses, the business context is as important as the individual's name. Tools like Intercom, Salesforce, and others treat this as a first-class concept. PostHog's group analytics already models this relationship – surfacing it in person display names would make the whole product significantly more useful for B2B teams.

payload.author: sampennington
payload.body:
## Summary

A funnel that mixes a regular events series with a data-warehouse series fails the whole query with ClickHouse `Code: 386 ... no supertype for types UUID, String` (`NO_COMMON_TYPE`).

Surfaced from `system.query_log` analysis of failing product-analytics insight queries — ~46 occurrences / ~5 teams over 7 days. Tracked on the [Product analytics — insight query failures dashboard](https://metabase.prod-us.posthog.dev/dashboard/207-product-analytics-insight-query-failures).

## Root cause

The funnel `UNION ALL`s its series. The two series resolve `aggregation_target` to incompatible types:

```sql
-- Events series: person aggregation
if(not(empty(e__override.distinct_id)), e__override.person_id, e.person_id) AS aggregation_target  -- UUID
UNION ALL
-- Data-warehouse series
e.user_id AS aggregation_target  -- String
```

`UNION ALL` requires matching column types across branches. The events series produces a `UUID` (`person_id`); the data-warehouse series produces the warehouse `user_id` column (`String`). No common type → the query fails.

Relevant code: `posthog/hogql_queries/insights/funnels/funnel_event_query.py` — `_aggregation_target_expr()` (events path, resolves to `person_id` UUID) and the data-warehouse path (`parse_expr(table_entity.aggregation_target_field)`, a String).

## Proposed fix

When a funnel mixes a data-warehouse series with an events series, coerce every series' `aggregation_target` to a common type (`toString(...)`) so the `UNION ALL` is well-typed.

- For a mixed funnel the downstream actors query already has to cope with non-UUID actor ids (the data-warehouse series produces them), so `toString` is consistent there.
- A pure-events funnel must stay `UUID` — coercing unconditionally would break the persons-modal lookup (`person.id = actor_id`).

So the fix needs "mixed funnel" detection plus parity testing of the actors/persons drill-in. It deserves its own focused PR with funnel-area review rather than a blanket change.

## Repro

A `FunnelsQuery` with one `EventsNode` step and one `DataWarehouseNode` step where the warehouse table's id/user column is a string.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
payload.title: Mixed data-warehouse + events funnel fails with NO_COMMON_TYPE (UUID, String)

payload.body: ### Bug Description When using custom retention brackets, cells whose time window has not yet fully elapsed show 0% instead of being marked as in-progress (grayed out). This is misleading because it implies zero retention when data collection is simply incomplete. For example, with brackets [1, 3, 4, 8] weeks and a cohort starting Feb 1, 2026, the "weeks 9–16" bracket window doesn't close until May 24, 2026. Yet the cell shows 0% today (May 16) rather than indicating the period is still open. This behavior is inconsistent with individual period columns, which correctly gray out trailing cells when data collection is still in progress. ## How to reproduce 1. Create a retention insight using weekly period with custom brackets (e.g. [1, 3, 4, 8]). 2. Set the date range to the last 4 months. 3. Observe the column corresponding to the longest bracket (e.g. "weeks 9–16") for cohort rows where cohort_start + bracket_end_week × 7 > today. 4. Those cells show 0% instead of being flagged as in-progress. ## Additional context Individual period columns at the trailing edge of the table are correctly marked as in-progress when data is incomplete. The same logic does not appear to apply to custom bracket columns — a cell shows as complete (0%) as soon as any data could theoretically have been recorded, even if the bracket's full window hasn't elapsed. Suggested fix: a bracket cell should be treated as in-progress when cohort_start + bracket_end_week × 7 > today. ### Debug info ```shell - [x] PostHog Cloud, Debug information: Session: https://us.posthog.com/project/sTMFPsFhdP1Ssg/replay/019e3325-fa7b-7d95-b8d7-3e7b67169570?t=4066 Admin: http://go/adminOrgUS/019b4f1e-a2c0-0000-aecd-78a9ab9544bc (project ID 271787) - [ ] PostHog Hobby self-hosted with `docker compose`, version/commit: n.a. - [ ] PostHog self-hosted with Kubernetes (deprecated, see [`Sunsetting Kubernetes support`](https://posthog.com/blog/sunsetting-helm-support-posthog)), version/commit: n.a. ```

payload.author: praneya0028
payload.body:
## Bug description

PostHog shows a "Leave feature flag? Changes you made will be discarded." confirmation dialog when navigating away from a dirty feature flag form. The dialog itself has two bugs:

**Bug A — Dialog prompts twice on Cancel.** When the dialog appears and you click **Cancel**, the same dialog immediately re-appears. You have to click Cancel a second time to dismiss it.

**Bug B — Cancel still discards the data.** After clicking Cancel (twice), the navigation proceeds anyway and the form is wiped. Clicking Cancel is supposed to keep you on the page with your edits intact.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Go to the new feature flag page (`/feature_flags/new`) or any existing flag edit page.
2. Edit any field — key, name, a release condition, or a JSON payload.
3. Trigger a navigation away from the page (e.g. switch browser tabs / click elsewhere) so the confirm dialog appears.
4. Click **Cancel** in the "Leave feature flag? Changes you made will be discarded." dialog.

**Expected:** Stay on the page, all edits preserved.

**Actual:**
- The same dialog re-appears, requiring a second Cancel click (Bug A).
- After dismissing it, navigation proceeds anyway and all form edits are lost (Bug B).

Reproduced on PostHog Cloud (us.posthog.com) on 2026-05-15.

## Regression introduced by

This appears to be a regression from **#54692** ("feat(feature-flags): add unsaved changes warning on edit page", merged ~2026-04-30), which added a `beforeUnload` interceptor to `frontend/src/scenes/feature-flags/featureFlagLogic.ts`.

## Suspected root causes (from reading the code)

**Bug A — double prompt:** The new `beforeUnload` block in `featureFlagLogic.ts` does not have the tab-id / scene-tab-cache guard that `products/actions/frontend/logics/actionEditLogic.tsx` uses for the same scenario. In `actionEditLogic.tsx` the `beforeUnload.enabled` callback checks `sceneLogic` `activeTabId` vs the logic's own `props.tabId` and returns `false` for tab switches, with a comment explicitly noting "the logic stays mounted via the scene-logic cache". `featureFlagLogic` has no equivalent guard — it also doesn't import `sceneLogic`, `FeatureFlagLogicProps` has no `tabId`, and `key()` is keyed only by `id`. It also lacks the `logic.isMounted()` check that `actionEditLogic` has in its `enabled` callback.

**Bug B — Cancel still discards:** `urlToAction` in `featureFlagLogic.ts` calls `actions.loadFeatureFlag()` / `actions.resetFeatureFlag()` unconditionally on every `method === 'PUSH'`. None of those calls are guarded against `hasUnsavedChanges`. If any navigation reaches `urlToAction` even though the user clicked Cancel (the `beforeUnload.onConfirm` never ran), the form gets reset anyway and the edits are lost.

## Suggested fix

1. Mirror the `actionEditLogic.tsx` tab-id / scene-cache guard (and the `logic.isMounted()` check) in the `beforeUnload` block of `featureFlagLogic.ts`.
2. Guard the `loadFeatureFlag()` / `resetFeatureFlag()` calls in `urlToAction` so they don't run while there are unsaved changes (or move the reset into `beforeUnload.onConfirm` so it only runs when the user actually confirms).
3. Add a regression test in `featureFlagLogic.test.ts` alongside the existing `hasUnsavedChanges` tests, asserting that cancelling navigation preserves the form values.

I'm happy to send a PR for this. Before I do — `featureFlagLogic` currently has no `tabId` on its props, so wiring the tab-id guard the way `actionEditLogic` does would mean adding `tabId` to `FeatureFlagLogicProps` + `key()` + the scene mount. Would you prefer that approach, or is there a lighter-touch fix you'd rather I take for Bug A?
payload.title: Bug: "Leave feature flag?" dialog prompts twice and still discards data on Cancel

### Bug Description

During the setup flow using `npx @posthog/wizard`, the terminal screen starts flickering continuously from the beginning until when the UI is focused on the **Status** tab, following, until the setup is over.

Environment:

* OS: Debian on WSL2
* Kernel:

  ```text
  Linux TENRIPLEY 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu Jun 5 18:30:46 UTC 2025 x86_64 GNU/Linux
  ```
* Terminal: WezTerm
* WezTerm version: `20240203-110809-5046fc22`

The issue only happens on the **Status** tab. If I switch to other tabs such as **Event Plan** or any other tab in the wizard UI, the flickering stops immediately.

I will attach a video demonstrating the behavior.

### Bug Description

## Please describe
When a custom S3/GCS source uses Parquet files with native struct columns, PostHog's schema detector correctly identifies the nested structure and labels them as `JSON` type in the UI. However, ClickHouse reads Parquet structs as `Tuple` types internally, and HogQL's dot notation desugars to `JSONExtractRaw()`, which only operates on JSON strings. This means dot syntax like `customer.email` fails with:

> The first argument of function JSONExtractRaw should be a string containing JSON, illegal type: Tuple(...)

The expected behavior is that dot notation on these columns should work, since the schema UI shows them as JSON and the docs describe dot notation as the way to access nested data.

## How to reproduce

1. Upload a Parquet file to S3 where one or more columns contain native Parquet struct types (not serialized JSON strings).
2. Link it as a custom source in the data warehouse.
3. Observe the struct column shows as `JSON` type in the schema UI.
4. Run a query using dot notation on that column, e.g. `SELECT customer.email FROM my_table LIMIT 1`.
5. Query fails with the `JSONExtractRaw` / `illegal type: Tuple(...)` error.

`tupleElement(customer, 'email')` works as a workaround, confirming ClickHouse can access the data.

## Is your feature request related to a problem?

Annotations support markdown today: the content already renders through the same `TextContent` component used by dashboard text cards (see `frontend/src/lib/components/AnnotationsOverlay/AnnotationsOverlay.tsx:459`), and the input is `LemonTextAreaMarkdown` with a Preview tab. A customer plans to use annotations extensively to track correlations with product activity and reported that, without the rich editor, the input experience does not match what they get on text tiles.

## Describe the solution you'd like

Use `RichMarkdownEditor` (`frontend/src/lib/components/MarkdownEditor/rich/RichMarkdownEditor.tsx`) inside `AnnotationModal.tsx`, following the same lazy-load + legacy-fallback pattern used by `TextCardModalBodyField.tsx` so that existing annotations with non-roundtrippable markdown keep working.

Four decisions to make as part of the implementation (which are why I've raised this as a feature rather than doing it myself):

1. Character limit: cards use 4000, annotations cap at 400 today, the DB supports 8192. Pick the right value for annotations.
2. Modal sizing: `AnnotationModal` is `width={512}` and the rich editor defaults to `minRows=8, maxRows=20`. Either resize the modal or pass smaller min/max rows for annotations.
3. Markdown extension set: `TEXT_CARD_MARKDOWN_EXTENSIONS` is tuned for cards (tables, embeds, images). Annotations may want a narrower set (headings, lists, bold/italic, links, code).
4. Legacy fallback: replicate the `shouldUseLegacyMarkdownEditor` check from text cards so existing 400-char content that does not round-trip through TipTap is not corrupted on edit.

payload.author: rajuAhmed1705
payload.body:
## Problem
In SQL/HogQL insight result tables, cell values are visually truncated when the
content is long. This makes the table view unreadable for any insight that
surfaces longer strings — e.g. message transcripts, LLM tool-call arguments,
error stack traces, raw event payloads.

There is currently no way to view the full cell value inside the PostHog UI:

- Wrapping the value in `map(...)` or `tuple(...)` still truncates the inner
  string.
- Cell hover doesn't show the full value.
- Clicking the cell or row doesn't open a detail panel.
- The only reliable way to read the full content is exporting the entire
  result to CSV/JSON — which is overkill when you just want to read one row,
  and breaks the in-context workflow of pivoting/filtering inside PostHog.

## Use case
We use SQL insights to render LLM chat transcripts joined with tool-call /
tool-response events (one row per turn, ordered by timestamp). The \"content\"
column holds messages of 100–2000 characters. Today, we can only read the
first ~80 chars of every message inside the PostHog UI, so the insight is
useful for filtering/sorting but not for actually reading what was said.

This pattern (AI-generated content, audit logs, transcripts) is likely to
become more common as PostHog is increasingly used for LLM observability.

## Proposed behaviour
Any of these would solve it:

1. **Row detail side panel** — clicking anywhere on a row in a SQL insight
   opens a side panel listing every column with the full, untruncated value
   (similar to the event-detail panel in the Events explorer).
2. **Cell expand-on-click** — clicking a truncated cell opens a popover/modal
   with the full value, with a copy-to-clipboard affordance.
3. **Column display setting** — per-column \"wrap text\" / \"expand by default\"
   toggle in the insight's display config.

Option 1 would be the most generally useful and matches how the Events tab
already handles long property values.

## Workarounds tried
- \`map('text', long_string)\` — still truncates.
- \`tuple(long_string)\` — still truncates.
- \`toJSONString(...)\` — still truncates.
- CSV export — works, but disrupts the analysis loop.
- Browser DevTools \"Inspect element\" on the cell — works, but obviously not a
  real solution.

## Environment
PostHog Cloud (EU), saved SQL insight on a HogQL query.
payload.title: SQL insight: ability to view full untruncated cell value (row detail / click-to-expand)

payload.author: lazybios
payload.body:
## Summary

On a fresh Hobby self-hosted deployment (latest `master`), `$exception` events go in but never come out: `events` table stays at `0`, `error_tracking_*` tables stay at `0`, the Error Tracking UI shows "No Exception events have been detected!" forever.

The `cymbal` and `ingestion-error-tracking` containers are both `Up` but completely idle.

The reason is that `docker-compose.base.yml` doesn't pass two environment variables that the rest of the stack assumes are set. Both are set explicitly in the `bin/start-rust-service` and `bin/start` local-dev launchers, but those launchers aren't used in the docker-compose path.

Adding two lines to `docker-compose.base.yml` fixes the whole pipeline.

---

## Environment

- Deployment: `docker-compose.hobby.yml` extending `docker-compose.base.yml`, latest `master`
- `capture` image: `ghcr.io/posthog/posthog/capture:master` (built at commit `8d12f459aa312f7ff967edf5535607494d659e71`)
- `cymbal`: healthy, listening on `0.0.0.0:3302`
- `ingestion-error-tracking`: healthy, "All systems go in 134ms"
- All Kafka topics auto-created (`error_tracking_events` AND `ingestion-errortracking-main`)
- Project setting `autocapture_exceptions_opt_in = True`

---

## Root cause (verified end-to-end)

### Defect 1: `capture` writes to the wrong topic

`rust/capture/src/config.rs` defaults `kafka_error_tracking_topic` to `"error_tracking_events"`:

```rust
#[envconfig(default = "error_tracking_events")]
pub kafka_error_tracking_topic: String,
```

But the consumer side (`nodejs/src/config/kafka-topics.ts`) consumes a different topic:

```typescript
KAFKA_ERROR_TRACKING_INGESTION = `${prefix}ingestion-errortracking-main${suffix}`
```

`bin/start-rust-service` knows about this and explicitly bridges the gap:

```bash
# bin/start-rust-service:52
export KAFKA_ERROR_TRACKING_TOPIC=${KAFKA_ERROR_TRACKING_TOPIC:-ingestion-errortracking-main}
```

But `docker-compose.base.yml`'s `capture` service doesn't:

```yaml
capture:
    environment:
        ADDRESS: '0.0.0.0:3000'
        KAFKA_TOPIC: 'events_plugin_ingestion'
        KAFKA_HOSTS: 'kafka:9092'
        REDIS_URL: 'redis://redis7:6379/'
        CAPTURE_MODE: events
        RUST_LOG: 'info,rdkafka=warn'
        # ← no KAFKA_ERROR_TRACKING_TOPIC
```

So the `rust capture` service routes `$exception` events to a topic (`error_tracking_events`) that nothing in the stack consumes, while `ingestion-errortracking-main` stays at `LOG-END-OFFSET=0` forever.

### Defect 2: `ingestion-error-tracking` calls cymbal at the wrong host

`nodejs/src/ingestion/error-tracking/config.ts` defaults `ERROR_TRACKING_CYMBAL_BASE_URL` to `http://localhost:3302`:

```typescript
ERROR_TRACKING_CYMBAL_BASE_URL: 'http://localhost:3302',
```

That's correct for monolithic local dev (`bin/start` sets it explicitly to `http://lvh.me:3302`):

```bash
# bin/start
# Error tracking — Node.js ingestion consumer needs to reach Cymbal (Rust) on the host
# Using lvh.me instead of localhost for cross-platform compatibility
export ERROR_TRACKING_CYMBAL_BASE_URL=${ERROR_TRACKING_CYMBAL_BASE_URL:-http://lvh.me:3302}
```

But in docker-compose, `cymbal` is a separate container and Compose's network DNS exposes it as `cymbal:3302`, not `localhost:3302`. `docker-compose.base.yml` doesn't set this either:

```yaml
ingestion-error-tracking:
    command: node nodejs/dist/index.js
    restart: on-failure
    environment:
        PLUGIN_SERVER_MODE: 'ingestion-errortracking'
        DATABASE_URL: '...'
        KAFKA_HOSTS: 'kafka:9092'
        REDIS_URL: 'redis://redis7:6379/'
        # ← no ERROR_TRACKING_CYMBAL_BASE_URL
```

This silently breaks anyway because, with Defect 1 in place, the consumer never receives a message and never tries to call cymbal — so the misconfiguration goes unnoticed until you fix Defect 1, and then it surfaces as a graceful-shutdown loop.

---

## Reproduction

1. `git clone posthog && cd posthog && docker compose -f docker-compose.hobby.yml up -d`
2. Wait for `posthog-cy
payload.title: Hobby self-hosted: docker-compose.base.yml is missing two ENVs that error tracking needs end-to-end

payload.author: lazybios
payload.body:
## Bug Description

After `bin/deploy-hobby` succeeds (all containers `Up`, `/_health` returns `ok`), the admin onboarding `/preflight` page reports:

- **Plugin server · Node — Error** (downgraded to *Warning* if "Just experimenting" mode is selected)
- **Queue · Kafka — Error**

Both checks are **false positives**:

- **Plugin server** — `root-ingestion-general-1` logs show `[INGESTION-V2-COMBINED] 🚀 All systems go in 617ms` and `librdkafka consumer subscribed`; the HTTP health endpoint on port 6738 responds; events captured through `/e/` flow into ClickHouse normally.
- **Kafka** — the broker is reachable from every Node service; producers and consumers all connect and process messages.

So the user sees red `Error` badges on the very first screen of self-hosted onboarding, even though the stack is fully functional. This produces a poor first impression and consumes time triaging non-issues.

## Root cause (partially known)

For the plugin server, this matches what's described in #53405 (Hobby Self-Host Dirty Dozen, Issue 10): Django's `is_plugin_server_alive()` reads Redis key `@posthog-plugin-server/ping`, but the heartbeat writer was removed from the Node image. The key is always `nil`, so the check always fails — even when the plugin server is healthy.

The Kafka check appears to follow a similar "the frontend / `health.py` expectation drifted away from what the new images expose" pattern, but I couldn't pinpoint the exact check function — `posthog/health.py` no longer defines an `is_kafka_*` helper, only `is_postgres_connected` / `is_clickhouse_connected` / `is_celery_broker_connected` / `is_cache_backend_connected`. So whichever code drives the "Queue · Kafka" preflight tile is either elsewhere or has been removed without updating the UI.

## How to reproduce

1. `bin/deploy-hobby latest <domain>` on a fresh VPS.
2. Wait for `/_health` → `ok`.
3. Open `/preflight` in the admin onboarding wizard.
4. Observe Plugin server and Kafka both marked Error, even though logs show both services healthy.

## Workaround

- Plugin server: spoof the heartbeat from a host cron — `* * * * * docker exec <redis-container> redis-cli SET "@posthog-plugin-server/ping" "$(date +%s)" EX 90 >/dev/null`. Preflight then turns green for that row.
- Kafka: no workaround found from outside the codebase; user must skip the preflight wizard (e.g., navigate directly to `/signup`).

## Suggested fix

- Replace the dead Redis heartbeat with an HTTP probe against the plugin server's `:6738` health endpoint (which is what the Node side already exposes).
- Audit the `is_*` functions in `posthog/health.py` against what the current `posthog/posthog-node:latest` image actually publishes; remove or update checks that no longer match reality (or re-add an `is_kafka_*` that talks to the broker directly).
- Until preflight is honest, the wizard should make it obvious that these particular failures don't block onboarding — or route around them automatically.

## Debug info

- [ ] PostHog Cloud
- [x] PostHog Hobby self-hosted with `docker compose`, image: `posthog/posthog:latest` (commit `2622588f5c`)
- [ ] PostHog self-hosted with Kubernetes
- Compose: `docker-compose.hobby.yml` + `docker-compose.base.yml`, generated by `bin/deploy-hobby`
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04 cloud VPS, 4 vCPU / 16 GB RAM

---
Thanks for maintaining PostHog — happy to verify any patches.
payload.title: Hobby preflight: "Plugin server · Node" and "Queue · Kafka" report Error despite both services healthy and processing events

payload.author: lazybios
payload.body:
## Bug Description

After running `bin/deploy-hobby` and waiting for migrations, the deployed instance returns HTTP 200 on `/_health` but the SPA shows a blank page for users on networks where per-stream throughput to the host is limited (typical for cross-region access, capped uplinks, or shared connections).

The root cause is **how `/static/*.js` chunks are served**. The default Caddyfile reverse-proxies `/static/*` to the `web` container, where NGINX Unit serves the file via the Django app. Two large entry chunks each weigh **8+ MB** uncompressed:

| File | Raw size |
|---|---|
| `staticfiles/chunk-PHKJLKH7.js` (hash will vary per build) | ~8.5 MB |
| `staticfiles/chunk-I2FYEAVV.js` (hash will vary per build) | ~8.2 MB |

Tests against the same instance show a **~100× difference** between the two serving paths:

| Path | Single-file download time (8.5 MB chunk) |
|---|---|
| Caddy → reverse_proxy `web:8000` (NGINX Unit) | 30+ s, frequently timing out |
| Caddy `file_server` direct, `precompressed br gzip` (2.1 MB after brotli) | **0.27 s** |

Because these chunks are required for the React entry to mount, the SPA never renders until they finish — observed as a blank page that lasts 60–90 seconds (or never resolves) on slow links.

## How to reproduce

1. Deploy via `bin/deploy-hobby latest <domain>` on a fresh VPS.
2. From a client where the path to the host caps single-stream throughput (e.g., cross-continent, mobile network, shared office uplink), open the deployed URL.
3. DevTools → Network: observe the two largest `/static/chunk-*.js` files (~8 MB each) hanging for tens of seconds. React `#root` stays empty.

## Workaround (verified)

1. Pre-compress JS/CSS in the web image:
   ```bash
   find /code/staticfiles -maxdepth 1 \( -name "*.js" -o -name "*.css" \) \
        ! -name "*.br" ! -name "*.gz" ! -name "*.map" -print0 \
     | xargs -0 -P4 -I{} brotli -q 6 -k {}
   ```
2. Make `staticfiles` available to the proxy container (volume mount or `docker cp`).
3. In the Caddyfile, before the catch-all `handle { reverse_proxy web:8000 }`:
   ```caddyfile
   handle /static/* {
       uri strip_prefix /static
       root * /usr/share/caddy/staticfiles
       file_server { precompressed br gzip }
       header Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"
   }
   ```
4. `caddy reload`. Same chunks now serve at line speed; React renders in seconds.

## Suggested fix

- Either: have the official image emit `*.br` and `*.gz` alongside every `staticfiles/*.{js,css}` at build time, **and** update `docker-compose.hobby.yml` so the proxy container can `file_server precompressed` directly; or
- Configure NGINX Unit to do `Accept-Encoding`-aware static serving (Unit ≥ 1.30 supports this) so the reverse-proxy path is no longer the bottleneck.

The current default makes hobby deployments effectively unusable for any audience whose network can't sustain ~25 MB of single-stream JS within typical browser stream timeouts.

## Debug info

- [ ] PostHog Cloud
- [x] PostHog Hobby self-hosted with `docker compose`, image: `posthog/posthog:latest` (commit `2622588f5c`)
- [ ] PostHog self-hosted with Kubernetes
- Compose: `docker-compose.hobby.yml` + `docker-compose.base.yml`, generated by `bin/deploy-hobby`
- Proxy: stock `caddy` image, configuration generated from `CADDYFILE` env var
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04 cloud VPS, 4 vCPU / 16 GB RAM

---
Thanks for maintaining PostHog and the deploy-hobby script — happy to test patches.
payload.title: Hobby self-hosted: NGINX Unit serves large /static/ chunks ~100x slower than Caddy file_server (blank page after deploy)

payload.author: MattBro
payload.body:
## Bug

Revenue Analytics' subscription, customer, and LTV charts can be wrong when the data warehouse holds stale Stripe subscription rows. Subs canceled after their initial sync stay counted as active forever; churn never increments; LTV stays empty. MRR / Gross revenue look correct.

## Repro

1. Set up a Stripe data warehouse source with the default Subscription schema (append-only incremental, keyed on `created`).
2. Have at least one subscription that gets canceled in Stripe after it was first synced.
3. Open Revenue Analytics, look at any period after the cancellation.

Expected: the canceled sub falls out of "active" and appears in churn after its `ended_at`.
Actual: it stays counted as active forever; churn never increments; LTV chart is empty.

## Root cause

Stripe subscription sync is append-only by `created` timestamp (`posthog/temporal/data_imports/sources/stripe/settings.py:78`, `source.py:262` - `supports_incremental=False`, `supports_append=True`). The DWH only fetches subs with new `created` values; existing rows are never re-fetched. When Stripe populates `ended_at` on cancellation, our copy of the row stays with `ended_at = NULL`.

The Revenue Analytics subscription view passes `ended_at` straight through (`products/revenue_analytics/backend/views/sources/stripe/subscription.py:55`), and the metrics query treats `NULL ended_at` as still active (`_period_gteq_expr` in `revenue_analytics_query_runner.py:469-482` short-circuits to true when `isNull(left)`).

Result:
- Subscription / customer counts inflate as canceled subs accumulate
- Churn check (`_period_eq_expr` on `ended_at`) never fires, so `churned_customer_count = 0`
- LTV `multiIf` returns `NULL` when `churned_customer_count = 0`, so the series is empty (`revenue_analytics_metrics_query_runner.py:204-209`)

MRR is unaffected because it's driven by invoices; when billing stops, no new invoices arrive and MRR drops naturally.

## Fix options

1. Add a merge / upsert sync mode for Stripe subscriptions in the data warehouse so existing rows update.
2. Auto-schedule periodic full refresh of the Subscription schema as a workaround.
3. Land the durable fix in Customer Analytics if Revenue Analytics stays in maintenance mode.

Customer workaround today: trigger a full refresh on the Subscription schema in DWH settings, and repeat periodically.
payload.title: Revenue Analytics counts canceled Stripe subscriptions as active when subscription rows are stale

payload.author: arthurdedeus
payload.body:
Let's build a dedicated model to hold our CSP/CRM-specific data instead of stuffing everything into groups.

The goal is to keep this as flexible as possible and, as we confirm solid use cases, commit with more performant/reliable approaches. E.g.:
- CSM/AE/Owner assignment in `properties` JSONB field rather than foreign keys to `user`: less performant/consistent than a foreign key, but keeps the schema flexible. We can always add the foreign key later on, but removing an existing field is more painful.
- Group/group type relationship in `properties`: still not sure if N-groups:1-account is a concrete use case, so let's defer the decision. JSONB schema gives us the flexibility.

**Note**: `properties` schema should be enforced through Pydantic. Users won't be able to add ad-hoc properties to it, the data living in there must be controlled.

# Accounts vs Groups

## Decision

Customer-relationship data (CSM, AE, owner, group attachments) lives on a new `Account` model rather than on `Group`.

## Why

Group is an analytical primitive entity, coupled to events and ingestion. Changing group's data invariably requires syncing Persons DB + Clickhouse (through ingestion pipeline). Due to the distributed DB nature, foreign keys between Groups and other tables that live outside Persons db are soft (not enforced by the db).

Decoupling Accounts from Groups also enables us to build "groupless accounts". This is useful to track deals/prospects once we start building more into the CRM direction. After a prospect converts, we link them to an analytical Group to track their usage/behavior.

We need more control over Account creation than we need for groups: these should be curated organizations the CSMs and AEs are in contact with. Being at the mercy of duplicated Accounts being created due to instrumentation errors, e.g., is not acceptable. Furthermore, Account may serve as a deduplicator for Groups, relating to N groups as a way of aggregating their data.

DevEx must not be overlooked here. Having a dedicated model without the overload Groups model currently has speeds up development significantly, as we can steer the new, still-unused model more easily than the extensively used Group model.

## What we're paying

- A new model, migrations, API, and eventual UI.
- Figuring out a workflow to create Accounts
- Need to connect Accounts to Groups in order to get behavioral/analytical data
payload.title: Customer analytics account data model

Decider: @liamg-posthog
What's the decision: Which social media pivots we will act on immediately
Planned date for decision: May 14

## Request for Comments: Immediate changes to PostHog's social media channels
I've been on the team for less than two weeks, so don't want to come in taking a machete to things before the guy that hired me and I've had our first day together (heyo).

*However, in the name of shipping fast, I have 3 things I would like to change at once about our social media presence. **Please think of this less as a "I need in-depth thoughts, this is high-level strategy" and moreso "I'm gonna do these minor changes anyways, are there any flags I should be aware of?"***

## The goal of this RFC's to:

Flag any problems with the proposed changes
Understand, through prompting in this thread, what preexisting assumptions I have that are wrong about PostHog social. 

## The expected output is:

Changes made to "optimize" our social channels
Video team having a clearer understanding of how we can repurpose long-form content on other channels


### 1. Naming conventions
I'll start with the most simple: all social media handles should be @PostHog

I totally get the thinking behind having 'team' or '.com' on the handle depending on the goal. However, being async we will never have enough BTS content to fill a feed, and let's be honest, only we care about that anyways.

Having all of our accounts (dormant or not) as @PostHog makes sense in every context. I want to do this ASAP: that means changing Instagram and Bluesky today.

This will require us to check through where we link our social accounts (website, email footers, etc) and update what's needed. While we're making those changes, we can add Threads and Bluesky to our "Like and subscribe" website dropdown.

### 2. Short-form video templates
We have a smart and creative as heck video team. We need to maximize the amount we can drive to YouTube for the long-form stuff they're creating, and use what they've already created well.

As such, I'm proposing

- One short-form video excerpt (30-40 seconds max) created for suitable long-form vids that'll go on YouTube, cut in both 9:16 and 1:1, with consistently-styled captions in bottom 3/4 of the screen.

9:16 is necessary to go out on Instagram, and works well for LinkedIn as well
1:1 is 'optimal' for X/Twitter because only 20% of our profile visits, 25% of our impressions, and 6% of our shares from the platform are on desktop. The rest are on mobile.
If our main KPI for X/Twitter is impressions, we need to optimize for where those new ones are coming from: people scrolling on their phones. 1:1 works well for both mobile and desktop, and a lot of people who create videos for the site specifically prioritize that aspect ratio for that reason.

The team are already doing this, we just need to align on the specs, proposed above.

### 3. Article-to-IG pipeline
Speaking of Instagram, we need to get our written-content-to-IG pipeline going. I see the process looking like this:

a) Written blog copy finalized

b) Art request for the blog includes both banner and 5-panel 4:5 image set.
Image 1 will be the blog's title and creative artwork.
Image 2, 3 and 4 will be the most relevant and curiosity-inducing excerpts, 200 characters, max.
Image 5 will be a CTA of "Sign up for build mode, the world's only newsletter for product builders that doesn't suck" and the PostHog logo.
Once the 'template' is created, the text input can be tweaked by me or whoever's doing the posting.

c) ManyChat flow is created that enables users to comment a key word and be sent a link to the full article. We can also prompt them to sign up for the newsletter in the DMs if we would like.

Daniel would be the one to create each of these and I've already spoken to him about what this sort of template would look like.

## Impact on teams
These changes are small and quick from our side on editorial, but will mean more time editing for team YouTube, and add another

payload.body:
### Bug Description

## Please describe
When a user transitions from opted-in to opted-out via `opt_out_capturing()` with `cookieless_mode: "on_reject"`, the session manager is torn down but rrweb observer hooks (e.g. mousemove callbacks) remain active. When those callbacks fire, they try to access `_sessionManager`, which no longer exists, and throw:

```
Uncaught Error: [SessionRecording] must be started with a valid sessionManager.
    at get _sessionManager (lazy-loaded-session-recorder.ts:386:19)
    at _updateWindowAndSessionIds (lazy-loaded-session-recorder.ts:1519:46)
    at onRRwebEmit (lazy-loaded-session-recorder.ts:1117:18)
```


## How to reproduce

1. Initialize posthog-js with `cookieless_mode: "on_reject"` and `persistence: "memory"`.
2. User accepts cookies: call `posthog.set_config({ persistence: "localStorage+cookie" })` then `posthog.opt_in_capturing()`. Session recording starts normally.
3. User later revokes consent: call `posthog.opt_out_capturing()`. The `reset` fires and tears down the session manager, but rrweb's observer hooks are still active.
4. Any mouse movement after step 3 triggers the error.

Expected: `opt_out_capturing()` should stop session recording (and tear down rrweb observers) before the session manager is destroyed.


## Additional context
From: https://posthoghelp.zendesk.com/agent/tickets/57057 (moved to PostHog: https://us.posthog.com/project/2/support/tickets/58794)

### Debug info

```shell
Debug info

Admin: http://go/adminOrgEU/019b2be2-5563-0000-6408-1e45bbe55e38 (project ID 109289)
```

payload.author: sdginty
payload.body:
### Bug Description

  Bug description

  The personal API key creation/edit UI at /settings/user-api-keys does not list the file_system scope, even though it is a valid backend scope documented at posthog.com/docs/api/file-system (which states
  file_system:read is required to call those endpoints).

  This means there is no way through the UI to create a key scoped specifically to file_system — users have to either grant * (full access) or patch the key's scopes array via the API directly, which
  defeats the security best-practice guidance in the docs.

  Root cause

  The frontend maintains a hardcoded API_SCOPES array in frontend/src/lib/scopes.tsx that has drifted from the backend's APIScopeObject definition in posthog/scopes.py. Several backend scopes are missing
  from the UI list:

  - file_system
  - file_system_shortcut
  - batch_import
  - conversation
  - event_filter
  - external_data_schema
  - link
  - persisted_folder
  - streamlit_app
  - tagger
  - warehouse_objects
  - notebook (double-check — may already exist)

  (List derived by diffing the backend scope objects against the frontend API_SCOPES array on master.)

  Steps to reproduce

  1. Go to Settings → Personal API keys → Create a personal API key
  2. Try to find a File system toggle in the scope list
  3. Observe it is not present, despite being required per the File API docs

  Expected

  file_system (and the other missing scopes) should be selectable as read/write in the UI, matching the backend.

  Workaround

  PATCH the key via the API:

  curl -X PATCH https://<host>/api/personal_api_keys/<KEY_ID>/ \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY_WITH_USER_WRITE>" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"scopes": ["file_system:read", "file_system:write"]}'

  The backend accepts this — the gap is purely in the frontend list.

  Suggested fix

  Either (a) generate the frontend API_SCOPES list from the backend APIScopeObject definition so they cannot drift, or (b) add the missing scopes manually and add a CI check that diffs the two lists.


### Debug info

```shell
- [X] PostHog Cloud, Debug information: Session: https://us.posthog.com/project/sTMFPsFhdP1Ssg/replay/019e0296-0d2a-72f1-a2ee-0c94b79cbf82?t=355
Admin: http://go/adminOrgEU/019763b5-4715-0000-2244-e95c0efb490f (project ID 74603)
```
payload.title: file_system (and other) scopes missing from personal API key UI

payload.author: andrewm4894
payload.body:
Tracking issue for the **Signals scout v1** build — a scheduled headless scout that proactively explores a PostHog project, writes durable scratchpad entries across runs, and emits findings into the Signals inbox via a `signals_scout` / `cross_source_issue` source variant.

Use this issue as the entry point for the work in progress; per-PR review happens on the linked PRs.

> **Naming note.** What was originally the "Signals agent" was renamed to the "Signals scout" (and durable cross-run "memory" to "scratchpad") in the 2026-05-18 rename — Python / DB / MCP / URL surfaces all use `scout` / `scratchpad` now (`SignalScoutConfig`, `SignalScoutRun`, `SignalScratchpad`, `scout_harness/`, `signals-scout-*` skills + MCP tools, `signals_scout` source variant, `signal_scout[:_internal]` scopes). The internal navigator skill in the PostHog Skills Store keeps the `signals-agent` name for muscle-memory continuity.

## What it is

The signals scout runs on an hourly Temporal schedule. For each enabled team, the coordinator samples `runs_per_tick` (default 1) `signals-scout-*` skills uniformly at random without replacement, spawns a sandboxed scout run per sampled skill, and lets the scout decide what to investigate. Findings flow back into the existing signals pipeline as `cross_source_issue` signals — the same emitter → buffer → grouping path as any other signal source.

A "scout fleet" model ships in v1:

- `signals-scout-general` — cross-product generalist. A lean 3-file skill: a thin `SKILL.md` navigation surface plus two on-demand references — `references/emit.md` (the emit contract: payload schema, weight / confidence rubrics, severity, dedupe keys, worked example) and `references/conventions.md` (scratchpad key prefixes, the four-states dedupe classifier, cross-project noise patterns). Its job is cross-product correlation; per-product surfaces are owned by the specialists.
- 7 specialists — `signals-scout-llm-analytics`, `-logs`, `-error-tracking`, `-revenue-analytics`, `-surveys`, `-observability-gaps`, `-csp-violations`. Each is a single self-contained `SKILL.md`.
  - Most watch for _anomalies_ in their domain.
  - `-surveys` is hybrid: anomaly watch on rating / response-rate / abandonment plus theme aggregation on open-text responses.
  - `-observability-gaps` watches for _structural gaps_ between events firing and existing insight / dashboard / alert coverage, and emits P3 _recommendations_ rather than problem alerts.

The scout fleet is also the first example of PostHog shipping templated default skills into a user's PostHog Skills Store via `lazy_seed` — users can edit them per-team and the harness preserves the divergence.

## Why this shape for v1

The scout is **pull-based** and sends findings into `emit_signal()` as a new source rather than acting on reports directly. A few reasons this is the right v1 shape:

- **Leans into the existing pipeline.** Scout findings flow through the same emitter → buffer → grouping → report path as every other signal source. No parallel ingest path; no special-case rendering, storage, or downstream behavior.
- **Scout mode bolts onto the edges.** The harness owns one well-scoped concern (deciding what's worth a closer look and emitting findings). The existing report-generation path owns acting on those findings once they're grouped. The two layers compose without either knowing about the other, which keeps both halves much easier to reason about.
- **Users can join in via their own "skills as scouts".** Authoring a new `signals-scout-foo/SKILL.md` is the only thing required to add a new scout — `lazy_seed` mirrors it onto the team's `LLMSkill` rows and the coordinator picks it up on the next tick. No coordinator-side wiring, no new model fields.

A future version could let the scout drive report generation directly (skipping the emit-and-group hop). That is a meaningfully bigger scope change and is best done once the v1 emit-only loop has been validated end-to-end.

## Architecture & docs
payload.title: Tracking issue: Signals scouts v1 — headless scout for the signals inbox

### Bug Description

Fresh `deploy-hobby` install on a clean Hetzner VPS came up successfully, but the preflight gate blocked setup because **Queue - Kafka** and **Plugin server - Node** showed as failed.

The underlying services were actually healthy:
- `root-kafka-1` was `Up ... (healthy)`
- `root-ingestion-general-1` logged `Kafka ready` and `All systems go`
- `root-recording-api-1` logged `Started successfully` and `All systems go`
- the app served normally after bypassing the preflight page

The problem appears to be that PostHog's own preflight endpoint reports stale/incorrect status for Kafka/plugins in this self-hosted hobby deployment.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 VPS
2. Run the hobby installer from the docs:
   ```bash
   /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/posthog/HEAD/bin/deploy-hobby)"
   ```
3. Use a real public hostname with TLS
4. Wait for the stack to come up
5. Visit `/preflight`

### Expected Behavior

If Kafka / Node ingestion services are healthy, preflight should allow setup to continue.

### Actual Behavior

Preflight blocks setup and reports Kafka/plugins as failed even though the containers and logs show healthy startup.

### Debug info

Environment:
- Self-hosted hobby deploy with `deploy-hobby`
- Fresh VPS on Hetzner
- Ubuntu 24.04
- 4 vCPU / 16 GB RAM / 150 GB disk
- domain behind Cloudflare: `analytics.gameye.com`
- observed on May 6-7, 2026

Commit/UI info visible in the running app:
- `Commit: 60bd49b82d`

Preflight endpoint response from the running instance:
```json
{
  "django": true,
  "redis": true,
  "plugins": false,
  "celery": true,
  "clickhouse": true,
  "kafka": false,
  "db": true,
  "initiated": false,
  "cloud": false,
  "demo": false,
  "realm": "hosted-clickhouse",

  },

    "available": false,
    "client_id": null
  },
  "data_warehouse_integrations": {
    "hubspot": {"client_id": ""},
    "salesforce": {"client_id": ""}
  },
  "object_storage": true,
  "public_egress_ip_addresses": []
}
```

Relevant healthy service evidence:

`ingestion-general` after restart:
```text
[INGESTION-V2-COMBINED] 👍 Kafka ready
[INGESTION-V2-COMBINED] 🩺 HTTP server listening on port 6738
[INGESTION-V2-COMBINED] 🚀 All systems go in 688ms

`recording-api` after restart:
```text
[RECORDING-API] [RecordingApi] Started successfully

```

Container state at the time of the failure included:
- `root-kafka-1` healthy
- `root-feature-flags-1` healthy
- `root-web-1` up
- `root-ingestion-general-1` up
- `root-recording-api-1` up

Workaround:
- bypass the preflight page directly, then the app works normally

This feels similar to other recent hobby/self-host bootstrap issues, but in this case the stack is actually healthy and the blocker is the preflight gate/reporting itself.

payload.body:
### Bug Description

## Bug description

Commit `5357ae3b695` introduced `_insert_batch_via_personhog` in `posthog/models/cohort/cohort.py`, which added a new ClickHouse `SELECT` query (`_get_existing_ch_member_uuids`) to deduplicate persons before insertion. This query runs without `product`/`feature` query tags, triggering `UntaggedQueryError` in `DEBUG` mode.

The error is `DEBUG`-only so it does not affect production.

## How to reproduce

1. Run local dev environment with personhog enabled
2. Create a static cohort
3. Try to add persons to it via the UI or `PATCH /api/cohort/:id/add_persons`
4. Observe `500 Internal Server Error` with traceback ending at `posthog/models/cohort/cohort.py:848`

## Additional context

```
posthog.clickhouse.client.execute.UntaggedQueryError: sync_execute called with missing query tags: product, feature
  File "posthog/models/cohort/cohort.py", line 848, in _get_existing_ch_member_uuids
```

Root cause: `_get_existing_ch_member_uuids` calls `sync_execute` before `insert_static_cohort` (which already sets its own tags) gets a chance to run. Fix is to add `tag_queries(product=ProductKey.COHORTS, feature=Feature.COHORT)` in `_insert_batch_via_personhog` before the ClickHouse dedup check.

### Debug info

```shell
- [ ] PostHog Cloud, Debug information: [please copy/paste from https://us.posthog.com/settings/project-details#variables or https://eu.posthog.com/settings/project-details#variables]
- [x] PostHog Hobby self-hosted with `docker compose`, version/commit: ddf3ea88199088713a822ef064e1e58f44c50717
- [ ] PostHog self-hosted with Kubernetes (deprecated, see [`Sunsetting Kubernetes support`](https://posthog.com/blog/sunsetting-helm-support-posthog)), version/commit: [please provide]
```

When I'm working on improving my app, I'm focused on one dashboard at a time, and seeing all reports from all dashboards in the report list adds noise that is irrelevant.

 So ideally, in the filter menu alongside Status and Source, there could be a "Dashboard" filter where we can select the dashboard we care about and only see its reports.

I’m running a self-hosted PostHog hobby deployment on EC2 using the Docker Compose setup.

The disk usage is growing quickly, and after inspecting Docker volumes, Redpanda/Kafka seems to be the main source of disk usage, especially the `events_plugin_ingestion` topic.

payload.author: MattBro
payload.body:
## Context

[#57509](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/57509) adds \`llm_gateway:read\` (and \`dashboard:write\`, \`insight:write\`) to \`ALLOWED_PROVISIONING_SCOPES\` so partner OAuth tokens can request them. As written, the partner OAuth path does NOT check the \`gateway-personal-api-key\` feature flag that gates the same scope at the personal API key creation path (\`posthog/api/personal_api_key.py:92-111\`).

After #57509 ships, an org without the flag enabled (e.g. Insforge today) will be able to obtain a token with \`llm_gateway:read\` via partner OAuth, but won't be able to attach the same scope to a PAT. The two grant paths produce different results for the same org.

The flag was created by [@joshsny](https://github.com/joshsny) on 2026-01-15 (\`flag id 425428\`) with a single rule: \`email icontains @posthog.com\`, 100% rollout. It's been on for ~4 months in that state — a deliberate gate, not a forgotten rollout.

## Why the gate exists

The LLM Gateway proxies upstream Anthropic / OpenAI / etc. requests. PostHog covers the upstream cost (\`services/llm-gateway/src/llm_gateway/config.py:28\` shows a \$1000/day default product cost limit for \`llm_gateway\`). Granting \`llm_gateway:read\` is granting the right to burn through that limit. The team is being careful about who can run LLM spend via PostHog.

## The actual problem with the current design

The gate gates the wrong thing. It checks \"can this scope be granted to a token?\" but the spend happens at gateway request time, not at scope grant time. Gating one grant path (PAT) but not another (partner OAuth, post-#57509) doesn't control spend — it controls grant paths inconsistently.

## Recommended direction

Move the gate from PAT-creation to the LLM Gateway itself:

1. The gateway service checks the request's org against an allowlist (or billing-tier flag) at request time. Returns 402/403 with a clear reason if the org isn't entitled.
2. \`llm_gateway:read\` becomes a normal scope, grantable through any path (PAT, OAuth, partner OAuth) without a feature-flag conditional.
3. The PAT-creation conditional at \`posthog/api/personal_api_key.py:92-111\` gets removed.

Why this is better:

- **Spend is enforced where money actually flows.** The gateway is the mechanism; the scope is just a label. The gate belongs on the mechanism.
- **Grant paths converge.** Every path produces the same scope semantics. No surprises like \"partner OAuth bypasses what PAT enforces.\"
- **Billing tier becomes the natural gate.** Today's flag is a person-property check (\`email icontains @posthog.com\`). Tomorrow's billing tier is an organization-level fact. Putting the gate at the gateway lets it be checked against billing data directly.

## Decision needed before #57509 merges

Pick one:

**Option A — partner OAuth respects the existing PAT-level gate.** Add the same \`gateway-personal-api-key\` flag check to \`ALLOWED_PROVISIONING_SCOPES\` validation in \`ee/api/agentic_provisioning/views.py\`. Holds the line on grant-time gating until the structural fix lands. Inconsistency stays inside one decision (do all grant paths gate the same?), not silently across paths.

**Option B — drop the PAT-level gate; rely on gateway-side enforcement.** Move the gate as described above. The right long-term fix; small in code (one removed conditional, one added gateway-side check), but needs sign-off from whoever owns LLM spend control.

**Option C — keep the inconsistency, deliberately.** Document why partner OAuth bypasses the gate. Probably wrong, but state it explicitly if so.

If we ship #57509 without a decision, we ship Option C by default. Better to make the call explicitly.

## Related

- [Original Insforge thread](https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C0B0Q8UUL23/p1777920928699599)
- Flag: id 425428, owned by [@joshsny](https://github.com/joshsny), \`#team-platform-features\`
- Parent: [#57524](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/issues/57524)
- Blocks: [#57509](https://github.com/PostHog/

payload.body:
## Context

Per the [OAuth scope drift RFC's pre-flight #4](https://github.com/PostHog/requests-for-comments-internal/blob/matt/oauth-scope-drift-rfc/engineering/2026-05-04-oauth-scope-drift.md), PostHog's AS doesn't emit `invalid_scope` rejections to the standard log stream. They come back as HTTP 302 redirects with `?error=invalid_scope` in the redirect URL (per RFC 6749 § 4.1.2.1), but nothing logs the rejection on our side.

This means:
- The RFC's success criterion (\"zero `invalid_scope` over 30-day window\") is unmeasurable today
- We've been counting incidents by Slack reports + GitHub PRs, which is a lower bound
- Carmen's case (#57509) was caught manually in review, not surfaced by alerting

Confirmed via `query-logs` against `posthog-web-django`: zero results for searchTerm `invalid_scope` over the past 24h, despite the in-flight #57509 PR being the resolution to a customer-reported `invalid_scope` event in the same window.

## Change

In `posthog/api/oauth/views.py`, add structured logging at the point where the AS returns an `invalid_scope` redirect.

Two places to instrument depending on where DOT raises:
1. The `OAuthAuthorizationView` (or its parent in DOT) — when `validate_authorization_request()` raises `InvalidScopeError`
2. The exception handler that converts the OAuth error into the redirect URL

Add:

```python
import structlog
import posthoganalytics
logger = structlog.get_logger(__name__)

# At the rejection point:
logger.warning(
    \"oauth.authorize.invalid_scope\",
    requested_scopes=requested_scopes_list,
    grantable_scopes=grantable_scopes_list,
    missing_scopes=list(set(requested_scopes_list) - set(grantable_scopes_list)),
    client_id=request.GET.get(\"client_id\", \"\"),
    user_agent=request.headers.get(\"User-Agent\", \"\")[:200],
)
posthoganalytics.capture_exception(
    Exception(\"OAuth invalid_scope rejection\"),
    properties={
        \"missing_scopes\": list(set(requested_scopes_list) - set(grantable_scopes_list)),
        \"client_id\": request.GET.get(\"client_id\", \"\"),
    },
)
```

Confirm the `WARN`-severity Loki query produces results within 7 days of deploy.

## Acceptance

- A query like `SELECT count() FROM logs WHERE service.name = 'posthog-web-django' AND severity_text = 'warn' AND body ILIKE '%oauth.authorize.invalid_scope%'` produces non-zero results once a real rejection occurs
- The baseline metric for the RFC's success criterion is available within 7 days of this landing
- Capture in error tracking surfaces the spike if there's a regression

## Why

You can't measure what you don't observe. The RFC commits to \"zero `invalid_scope` over 30 days\" as the success metric for the structural cleanup; this issue makes that measurable.

## Tracking

## Context

Per the [OAuth scope drift RFC's pre-flight #2](https://github.com/PostHog/requests-for-comments-internal/blob/matt/oauth-scope-drift-rfc/engineering/2026-05-04-oauth-scope-drift.md), two of the 15 OAuth scope incidents in the last 90 days were drift between `posthog/scopes.py` `APIScopeObject` and the frontend's `API_SCOPES` descriptor map (surface 1↔6):

- [#47926](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/47926) — toolbar OAuth needed new scope objects added across `scopes.py`, `types.ts`, and `scopes.tsx` in lockstep
- [#56522](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/56522) — six scopes (`evaluation`, `live_debugger`, `llm_provider_key`, `revenue_analytics`, `tracing`, `web_analytics`) absent from `frontend/src/lib/scopes.tsx` `API_SCOPES`; consent screen rendered empty rows

`posthog/scopes.py` line 8-10 has a manual warning to keep these in sync with two frontend files. Manual warnings drift.

## Two ways to close this

### Option A: Invariant test (cheap, catches drift at PR time)

Add a Jest or pytest-equivalent test that asserts:

```ts
// frontend/src/lib/__tests__/scopes-coverage.test.ts (or similar)
import { API_SCOPES } from '../scopes'
import type { APIScopeObject } from '~/types'

// All scope objects from APIScopeObject Literal, minus internal-only
const ALL_SCOPES: APIScopeObject[] = /* derived from the Literal */
const INTERNAL = new Set(['clickhouse_test_cluster_perf', 'user_interview_DO_NOT_USE'])

test('every public APIScopeObject has an API_SCOPES entry', () => {
  const missing = ALL_SCOPES.filter(s => !INTERNAL.has(s) && !(s in API_SCOPES))
  expect(missing).toEqual([])
})
```

Runs in CI on every frontend change. Fails clearly with the named scope.

### Option B: Codegen (structural fix, eliminates drift)

Extend `hogli build:openapi` to generate the `API_SCOPES` descriptor map from `posthog/scopes.py`'s `get_scope_descriptions()` output (which is already the source for AS-published scopes). The descriptor map becomes a generated file like `frontend/src/lib/scopes.generated.ts`, paralleling the existing pattern at `services/mcp/src/lib/oauth-scopes.generated.ts` from #56835.

This is more work but matches the codegen pattern PostHog has chosen for OAuth scopes elsewhere.

## Recommendation

Option A first (5 min, immediate detection). File Option B as a separate follow-up for the structural fix.

## Tracking
